## 2026-06-19 (round 64) — activity `.interactive`: task-type completeness + multi-type marker scan (Chris, ENGS401) (build 260616.43)

Chris flagged (ENGS401-01 screenshot) that an activity holding an interactive widget should itself carry `.interactive`, "for EVERY SINGLE MODULE". Measured the human convention corpus-wide BEFORE coding → it is **per-TYPE, not blanket** → shipped the human-aligned completion of the round-58 post-pass (not a blanket rule, which would regress ~2,000 activities + the skeleton) → every protected gate held-or-improved (skeleton **+2** pages ≥50%).

- **Measured the convention (`outputs/_measure_activity_interactive_blanket.py` + number-matched `_measure_tasktype_convention.py`).** The human marks `.interactive` by the **kind** of widget inside: TASK widgets almost always (dragAndDrop 77–95%, typing 96%, selectionBox 89%, clickingOrder/crossword 100%, dropDown 64% ≈ the existing selfCheck 69% bar), DISPLAY widgets almost never (modal 12%, carousel 12%, tabs 15%, rotateBanner/speechBubble 17%, accordion 21%, flipCard 23%, clickDrop 24%). A true blanket "ANY interactive inside → `.interactive`" rule would flip ~2,000 display-widget activities AGAINST the human and regress the skeleton gate — declined with data, per the framework.
- **Two latent gaps found (both round-58 era).** (1) The post-pass marker regex `/INTERACTIVE \(un-built\) #\d+: (\w+)/` captured only the **FIRST** type of a multi-type placeholder banner — so an activity whose placeholder reads `"carousel + typing"` (display + task) never saw the task type → stayed plain. (2) The round-50 `interactive_widget_types` list predated several task widgets (dropDown/typing/selectionBox/clickingOrder/crossword), so those activities stayed plain even alone.
- **The fix (engine `ContentConverter.#activityInteractivePostpass`; data `activity_wrapper.interactive_widget_types`; env `ACTINT_OFF`).** (1) Widened the regex to `([\w +]+)` and split each banner on `" + "`, marking the activity `.interactive` if **any** member type is a task type. (2) Added the five measured task types to the data list (with an in-file `interactive_widget_types_round64_note` recording every percentage + the deliberate display-type exclusions). General + data-described — no per-module logic.
- **Result (verified in the regenerated corpus).** ENGS401-04 4A (`dropDown`) and ENGS401-05 5A (`carousel + typing`, now caught by the multi-type scan) flip from plain → `.interactive`, matching the human; display-only activities (ENGS401-02 2A `modal`, 2C `accordion + speechBubble`) correctly stay plain.
- **NOT fixed — a separate, deeper pass (reported honestly to Chris).** ENGS401-**01** activity 1A — Chris's exact example — stays plain, and correctly so under the type rule: triangulation (`ENGS401 …_parsed.txt` L113/L211/L332) shows its interactivity is a **prose-authored emotion-selection** ("Watch each clip… select the emotion that best matches how you feel"), while its `[modal]` tags are merely **video pop-ups** ("Battle" → a clip) and its carousel is display. Claude types both display widgets → plain. There is **no task TAG** to key off; the interactivity lives in prose. Fixing 1A needs a prose-selection classifier (recognise "select the … that best matches" + options → a selection task), sized + built as its own micro-round — NOT forced via a blanket rule that the measurement shows regresses the corpus.

**PROTECTED gates (full 197-set + OSSC301 regen, mtime-verified 0 stale / 1006 pages, corpus 198/1006):** **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD mean 47.0% — IMPROVED (pages ≥50% 375→377)**; literal-`[tag]` leak **545 / 181 — HELD**; structural-clean **825/1006 = 82.0% — HELD**; compare_structure **exact 4257 / EXTRA 111 / missing 190 — HELD** (a class on the activity div doesn't alter the wrapper chain); body_compare **ANY 128 (40/6/86) — HELD**; JS regression **0 / 9557 (100%) — HELD**; flipCard verifier **TOTAL 37 / divergence 0 — HELD**; carousel verifier **0 mismatched ids — HELD**. Data-flagged + `ACTINT_OFF` env A/B. (A post-regen documentation-only edit to the data note key — not read by the engine — is proven byte-identical via `diff -rq IDENTICAL`, so it is the §10 non-output-affecting case and does not stale the corpus, exactly like the AppVersion bump.)

## 2026-06-19 (round 57) — RED-NOTE SOURCE SPLIT: writer→Creative-Services notes prefixed "CS:", converter diagnostics keep "RED FLAG:" (build 260616.36)

Chris flagged (OSAI201-02 screenshot) that EVERY retained red note on the front-end was prefixed "RED FLAG:", conflating two unrelated sources: the writer's notes/questions to Creative Services, and the converter's own technical diagnostics. Relabel by SOURCE — a writer→CS instruction reads "CS:"; a CONVERTER_V2-could-not-render diagnostic keeps "RED FLAG:". Triangulated → measured corpus-wide → implemented behind a data flag + env toggle → gate-proven.

- **WT → human → Claude (the evidence, OSAI201-02).** WT `OSAI201 Writers Template_parsed.txt` line 304, the speechBubble image cell: `│ 🔴[RED TEXT] [image] CS [/RED TEXT]🔴*Give me* *three* *pet story ideas.* 🔴[RED TEXT] Can that text be on the sign? [/RED TEXT]🔴 / https://…gm1043483480 ║ … [speech bubble] Gen AI is a helpful tool…` — a documented `CS` cue after the `[image]` tag, then the writer's question "Can that text be on the sign?". Human gold `01-Finalized_Modules_/OSAI201/OSAI201-02.html`: NO red note (the designer strips them once v1 is built — framework §C). Claude round-56: `<p style="color: red">RED FLAG: Can that text be on the sign?</p>` (retained via the round-43 `#bundleInstructions` after the built bubble). Round-57: `<p style="color: red">CS: Can that text be on the sign?</p>` — same BOLD-RED `<p>`, prefix word only.

- **The discriminator (SOURCE, not content).** A WRITER-authored instruction span → "CS:": the round-43 retained-note family — `parse.class==="instruction"` / `instructionFragment` (the shared `Instruction_Cues.json` vocabulary: cs/csc/dev/note/please/can you…), the scanner's `bundle.instructions`, AND the undocumented container-positional note (`{tag} note: …`, the leftover from `#containerModifiers`). A CONVERTER-emitted technical diagnostic → "RED FLAG:": the hardcoded `#redFlag` messages where CONVERTER_V2 could not fully render the WT — empty/malformed tag, missing URL, orphan sub-tag, interactive-reached-unbundled, unmatched menu/container, un-built widget.

- **Measured corpus-wide BEFORE coding (`outputs/_measure_redflags.py`).** 4,639 retained notes across 860 pages split **3,669 writer→CS / 970 converter-diagnostic**. The 970 diagnostics are exactly the six firing hardcoded signatures (orphan-sub-tag 565, un-built-marker 190, no-URL 97, empty-callout 81, empty-heading 36, menu-no-tab 1; the two defensive sites never fire). The borderline `{tag} note:` class (122: alert 54 / activity 51 / important 2 / developer 6 / cs 1 / image 2 / video 4 / wananga 1 / supervisor-note 1) is writer guidance to the designer (positional "centre of page"/"rhs of"/"at bottom of"/"wide for interactives", build instructions "please create a tick…", explicit `developer note:`/`cs note:`/`Note to CS:` spans), NOT a conversion failure → CS. Only ~2.7% of writer notes (97) already lead with a CS/Dev/Note cue; their text is kept verbatim after the prefix (§4.1 unchanged), so e.g. `RED FLAG: CS: can a cross…` → `CS: CS: can a cross…` — the same double-label the prior form carried, not a new behaviour. Post-regen the corpus is **exactly 3,669 CS / 970 RED FLAG** with **0 diagnostics mis-routed to CS** and **0 writer notes left as RED FLAG**.

- **Implementation (data + flag + toggle).** `data/Emit_Templates.json` `red_flag`: new `cs_form` (`<p style="color: red">CS: {text}</p>`, styling identical to `form`) + `cs_relabel.enabled:true`. `ContentConverter.#redFlag(text, run, kind)` selects `cs_form` only when `kind==="cs"` AND `cs_relabel.enabled!==false` AND no `CSRELABEL_OFF` env — else `form`. The six writer-instruction call-sites pass `kind:"cs"`; the nine diagnostic sites default to "diagnostic". Env `CSRELABEL_OFF` (or `enabled:false`) reverts EVERY note to the round-43 all-"RED FLAG:" baseline. Greppability (§4.1) is preserved and sharpened: "RED FLAG:" now finds exactly the converter issues, "CS:" the writer notes.
- **Gate-filter parity (so a cosmetic rename can't move a gate).** `compare_structure.py` + `full_compare.py` exclude Claude's converter-added notes from the structural text match via `text.startswith("red flag")` (the human strips all such notes, so they have no counterpart). Extended both to also exclude `text.startswith("cs ")` — same intent, now both prefixes (`norm` strips the colon → "red flag" / "cs "). Without it the ~3,669 renamed notes would re-enter as unmatched Claude elements and spuriously drop the exact-chain %.

**PROTECTED gates (full 197-set + OSSC301 regen, STUB_OEMBED, mtime-verified 0 stale / 1006 pages):** literal-`[tag]` leak **602 / clean 80.2% — HELD** (note text unchanged → bracketed tags inside diagnostics counted identically); compare_structure **4251 exact / 80.0% + EXTRA-container 108 — HELD** (filter parity); JS regression **REAL FAILURES 0 / 100% (9557)**; flipCard **TOTAL 37 / defect 14 / divergence 0 — HELD, byte-identical to `outputs/baselines/flip_A.txt`**; **PRIMARY skeleton SCAFFOLD 47.0% (median 48.0%, pages ≥50% 46.0%) — HELD** (skeleton is text-stripped, so the prefix is invisible to it). A/B verified: under `CSRELABEL_OFF` the regenerated pages are byte-identical to the round-56 baseline (proven on OSAI201 + the 4 body_compare boundary modules). The relabel is structurally inert by construction.

**body_compare — over-capture 39→40 / ANY 128→129 (+1): a PROVEN non-structural note-length artifact, recorded honestly.** OVER-CAPTURE flags a page when `max_w/all_chars ≥ 0.40` (+ widget>400 chars + ≥3 lost blocks). "CS:" is 6 chars shorter than "RED FLAG:", so the developer-note text in `all_chars` (the ratio DENOMINATOR) shrank, nudging ONE page — **XMES103-01** — from raw ratio ~0.394 (rounds 0.39) to ~0.396 (rounds 0.40). Its numerator (`max_w` 2192) and `lost_blocks` (3) are unchanged: no widget boundary moved, no free block changed. Proven by A/B — reverting the four boundary modules with `CSRELABEL_OFF` restores **39 / 128** exactly. Per the round-50 MEASUREMENT MANDATE (skeleton + %-clean PRIMARY; the text-matched buckets "may shift… expected, not the gate" — round 54) this cosmetic-driven, sub-rounding shift is non-gating; the structural reality (five gates byte-identical) is that nothing structural changed. (Note: excluding the notes from `all_chars` would shrink the denominator further and flag MORE pages, so the metric's note-inflation is left as-is rather than "fixed" the wrong way.) Data-flagged + `CSRELABEL_OFF` reversible. Tools: `outputs/_measure_redflags.py`.

## 2026-06-18 (round 56) — FOUR OSAI201 fidelity fixes: list nesting, external-link button, speechBubble CS-isolation, glossary build (build 260616.35)

Chris flagged four distinct OSAI201 human↔Claude discrepancies in side-by-side screenshots, with a mandate to analyse them holistically (surrounding context + document flow, not just tag→tag). Each was triangulated (WT → human → Claude), fixed, and gate-proven in one round.

- **(1) LIST NESTING — `OSAI201-02` "What did we learn?".** WT: a 2-level bullet list (`• **Be specific**` at `w:ilvl` 0; `  • Bad prompt…` at ilvl 1). Human: `<ol><li><b>Be specific</b><ul><li>Bad prompt…</li><li>Good prompt…</li></ul></li>…</ol>` — a NUMBERED parent list with nested bullet children. Claude FLATTENED every bullet to one `<ul>` because **DocxExtractor dropped `w:ilvl` and `#renderBlackText` trimmed the indentation**. Fix: the extractor now captures `w:ilvl` and encodes it as leading 2-space indentation per level; `#renderBlackText` was rewritten to build nested `<ul>`/`<ol>` from the indentation (a recursive list builder), with an **OL-OVERRIDE** — a TOP-level bullet list whose every item is **bold** and carries nested sub-points renders as a numbered `<ol>` (the human's "category + sub-points" convention; the docx tags them bullets but `numId=3` is bullet at every level, so the numbering is the human's). Conservative: top level only, every item bold + parented, ≥2 items — a flat or non-bold list is byte-unchanged. Data `body_region.list_nesting`; env `LISTNEST_OFF`. Result: Claude now matches the human's nested `<ol>`/`<ul>` exactly.
- **(2) EXTERNAL-LINK BUTTON — `OSAI201-02` "Quick draw".** Human: `<a target="_blank"><div class="externalButton">…</div></a>` (class `externalButton`, measured 830 corpus-wide). Claude used class `button` AND, because the writer drops the marker INLINE mid-sentence ("Click here to play Quick Draw `[external link button]` https://… then come back and do the activity."), mislabelled the button with the trailing prose ("then come back and do the activity."). Fix (`ContentConverter.#element` + `Emit_Templates.buttons["external link button"]`): class → `externalButton`; the URL is extracted, a SHORT trailing phrase is the label else a derivable **default** ("Go to website", or "Go to video" for a video URL — the human's two dominant defaults), and the remaining trailing prose is **re-emitted as body** so it is neither lost nor mislabelled. (The exact editorial label "Quick, Draw!" is the game's proper name — not WT-derivable; the default is the reusable rule. The inline `[external link]` form, line 353, stays an inline `<a>` — the human renders 6,189 such inline external links, so it is correctly NOT a button; that page's button is editorial.)
- **(3) speechBubble CS-INSTRUCTION — `OSAI201-02` #12.** WT image cell: `[image] CS *Give me three pet story ideas.* [Can that text be on the sign?] / URL` — a documented CS cue after the `[image]` tag introduces a MANUAL-edit instruction (sign text + question, red AND black) that ran to the URL. The bubble stayed an un-built placeholder because `#stripDevSpans` can't remove the BLACK sign text, so the image cell carried 2 red spans + residual prose (the `#redSpanCount`/`imgResidual` guards bailed). Fix: `InteractiveBuilder.#isolateInstructionImageCell` reduces such a cell to its `[image]` tag + URL (the only build-relevant parts) when a cue sits directly after the tag — a normal image cell is untouched. The bubble now BUILDS (image + text), and the CS question is RETAINED as a red flag after the bubble (round-43 instruction-retention), not lost or leaked.
- **(4) GLOSSARY — `OSAI201-01`.** WT: `[glossary]` + flat "Term – Meaning" lines. Human: a Term/Meaning table inside the glossary box. Claude: an un-built placeholder (no builder) that also SWALLOWED the next `[H3]` "Types of AI". Fix: new `InteractiveBuilder.#glossary` (template `interactive_builders.glossary`) splits each captured line on the first en/em-dash and builds `<div class="glossary"><h3 class="glossaryTitle"><span>Glossary</span></h3><table class="table table-fixed search-table">` with a Term|Meaning header + one row per entry; the boundary bank's `glossary.heading_is_terminator` flipped `false→true` so the following `[H3]` renders as its own heading.

**PROTECTED gates (full 197-set + OSSC301 regen, mtime-verified 0 stale / 1006 pages; 0 h6 leaks; round-55 heading fix preserved):** literal-`[tag]` leak **602 / clean 80.2% — HELD**; compare_structure **4249→4251 exact / 80.0% + EXTRA-container 108 — HELD**; body_compare ANY-breakdown **128 — HELD** (OVER-CAPTURE 39 / RUNAWAY 6 / EMPTY 87); JS regression **REAL FAILURES 0 / 100%**; flipCard **divergence 0**; **speechBubble verifier 22 built / 0 defects** (incl. the newly-built #12); **skeleton SCAFFOLD 46.9→47.0%** (pages ≥50% 45.9→46.0%) — IMPROVED (nested lists + the two newly-built widgets move toward the human). ## 2026-06-18 (round 55) — HEADING HIERARCHY: body headings no longer render one level too deep (build 260616.34)

Chris flagged OSAI401-01: "What is Generative AI and LLM (large language model)?" renders as small body-sized text in Claude but as a full teal heading (peer to "Types of AI") in the human, and asked to fix the rendering by learning from the human's OVERALL heading hierarchy, not a straight tag translation. Triangulated → measured → two distinct causes found and fixed, both in `#relevelHeadings`.

- **WT → human → Claude (the evidence).** OSAI401 WT tags: "Types of AI" `[H3]`, "What is Generative AI…" `[H4]`, "How does it work?" `[H4]`, "AI Integration" `[H3]`; the activity titles "What can AI do"/"Match the AI Tool"/"Predict like AI!" are `[Activity N]`. The human renders the activity titles AND the `[H3]` sections all at **h3** (peers), and `[H4]` at **h4** — a flat 2-level outline. Claude rendered the activity titles at h3 but pushed `[H3]`→h4 and `[H4]`→h5, so "What is Generative AI…" came out h5 (small text). Measured corpus-wide (`outputs/_measure_headinglevel.py`): on 2,764 text-matched body headings Claude's LEVEL matched the human only **53.9%**, and **1,063 of 1,273 mismatches (83%) were Claude exactly ONE LEVEL TOO DEEP** (h4→h3 809, h5→h4 129, …) — a systematic flatten-the-human convention Claude missed.

- **Cause 1 — ACTIVITY-ANCHOR.** An activity title is emitted at a FIXED h3 (the top content-section level); a free-body `[H#]` heading is the writer digit + `body_shift` (+1). Round-45 re-levelling rank-normalises the page's DISTINCT free-body levels to h3-top — but it POOLED the activity h3 with the `[H#]` levels, so the activity h3 occupied the base rank and a peer `[H3]` section (emitted h4) stayed h4. **Fix:** treat activity subtrees like widget subtrees in `#relevelHeadings` (excluded from BOTH the level pool and the rewrite — `data heading_relevel.activity_anchor_classes: ["activity"]`; env `RELEVELACT_OFF`), so the free-body `[H#]` outline ranks from base on its own and the top `[H#]` aligns with the activity titles. SELF-SCOPING: only changes a page where an activity is the SHALLOWEST anchor (if a real free-body `[H2]`→h3 is present it already holds the base).

- **Cause 2 — CLAMP-COLLAPSE.** `body_shift` +1 then the h5 body clamp made `[H4]`→h5 and `[H5]`→h5 **collapse to the same level** before the re-leveller saw them, so a genuine 3-level page (OSAI401-04: human h3 "Data, data, data" > h4 "How AI uses data" > h5 "Data collection"…) lost its third level and the `[H5]` sub-items were pulled up to h4. **Fix:** when re-levelling is active, emit a writer `[H5]` at the intermediate **h6** (`data logical_to_element.relevel_headroom: 6`) so the re-leveller sees `{h4,h5,h6}` → ranks `{h3,h4,h5}` and reproduces the human's hierarchy; the h6 is intermediate-only (re-levelling always normalises it). A **SAFETY CLAMP** maps any h6 that survives inside a skip subtree (a widget/activity-internal `[H5]`) down to h5, so no h6 ever reaches output (verified 0 corpus-wide; with `RELEVEL_OFF` the emission ceiling stays h5).

- **Result.** OSAI401-01 now renders all 8 body headings at the human's levels (the four `[H3]` sections + activities at h3, the two `[H4]` at h4) — "What is Generative AI and LLM…?" is an h4 teal heading, matching the human; OSAI401-04's 3-level hierarchy is reproduced exactly (`[H5]` sub-items stay h5). Corpus-wide **heading LEVEL match 53.9% → 69.2%** (+421 headings; Claude-one-too-deep 1063 → 645). The combined fix is strictly better than activity-exclusion alone (sample 46.2% → 65.1% → 69.1%): the h6 headroom also removed the wrong-direction over-pull (sample claude-too-shallow 11→6, below baseline).

**PROTECTED gates (full 197-set + OSSC301 regen, mtime-verified 0 stale / 1006 pages; 0 h6 leaks).** Heading LEVEL never alters the row/col/activity wrapper chain, so the structural gates are gate-safe by construction: compare_structure **4249 exact / 80.0% + EXTRA-container 108 — HELD**; body_compare ANY-breakdown **128 — HELD**; literal-`[tag]` leak **602 / clean 80.2% — HELD**; JS regression **REAL FAILURES 0 / 100%**; flipCard **divergence 0** (TOTAL 37). **PRIMARY skeleton gate IMPROVED: SCAFFOLD 46.6 → 46.9%, pages ≥50% 44.6 → 45.9%** (heading levels are part of the skeleton, so matching the human's hierarchy raises it). Data-flagged + `RELEVELACT_OFF` / `RELEVEL_OFF` env A/B.

**Residual (measured, not this round):** the remaining one-too-deep cases are mostly `-00` overview pages where the human flattens `[H2]`+`[H3]` to all-h3 (no activity anchor — a different convention) and `h3→h2` cases where the human uses h2 below the h3 base floor. Sized for a later pass.

## 2026-06-18 (round 54) — DATA-TABLE CELL-TAG rendering: a structural [tag] inside a KEPT table cell renders inline, not as literal text (build 260616.33)

The cleanest remaining leak lever (round-53 diagnosis). A structural `[tag]` inside a cell of a **KEPT** `<table>` (one `#layoutTableGrid` did *not* un-table — a real DATA table, not a panel grid) leaked as literal text: Claude emitted `<th> [Body, bold]  <b>Line</b>` and `<td> [H2]  Organisation`. The human developer renders the tag INLINE, marker stripped. Triangulated, measured, implemented, gate-proven.

- **WT → human → Claude (the evidence).** ENGJ402-04 rhyme table, WT line 922 header `🔴[RED TEXT] [Body, bold] [/RED TEXT]🔴**Line** ║ … **Example** ║ … **Rhyme scheme…**` over plain data rows (`Line 1 ║ When I get home… ║ A`) → human `<th><b>Line</b></th>` (the `**` supplies the bold; the `[Body, bold]` tag is stripped); Claude leaked `<th> [Body, bold]  <b>Line</b>`. XGF9003-06 games matrix, WT line 1776 `🔴[RED TEXT] [H2] [/RED TEXT]🔴Organisation ║ Zingo!/…` → human `<td><b>Organisation</b></td>` (a DATA cell: bold ADDED) — but its header cell `[H2] Executive Function Skill / [Image] / url` → human `<th>Executive function skill</th>` (a HEADER cell: NO inner `<b>`, the `<th>` is already bold; the decorative icon image DROPPED). Claude leaked `<td> [H2]  Organisation` and `<th> [H2]  …/ [Image] / <a>url</a>`.
- **The human convention (derived from the OUTPUT, per the round-45 rule).** `[H1-6]` / `[Body, bold]` text → `<b>text</b>` in a **DATA** cell (`<td>`) but **PLAIN** text in a **HEADER** cell (`<th>`, already bold by default — verified the asymmetry on the XGF9003 matrix: same `[H2]` tag, `<td><b>…</b>` vs `<th>…</th>`). `[Body]`/`[Text]`/`[list]` → the text (no bold). An **image-only** cell → the in-cell `<img>`; a cell carrying a **text label AND a decorative `[Image]`** → the label, image dropped (the matrix header icon). The skeleton keeps inline `<b>`/`<a>`/`<img>` as nodes, so this th/td asymmetry + the dropped icon are real skeleton wins, not cosmetic.
- **Measured first (`outputs/_measure_celltag.py`).** In KEPT-table cells corpus-wide: **266 structural `[tag]` occurrences across 237 cells** (171 `<td>` / 66 `<th>`) — **113 image-only, 112 label-only, 12 label+image**. GUARD proven: the 34 widget-member-leading cells (`[front]`/`[Card N]`/`[Item N]`/`[Tab N]` → SUBTAG) and 231 bracketed-PROSE cells (`[tick]`, `[reading an internal staff noticeboard…]` → `Parse` returns null) are a cleanly separate set the structural-only scope cannot touch — so a genuine data table whose cells contain bracketed prose is never mis-rendered.
- **Fix (`ContentConverter.#renderCellInline`, called per cell from `#contentTable`; data `body_region.data_table_cell_tags`; env `CELLTAG_OFF`).** ACTIVATES only when a cell's LEADING part resolves (via `TagNormaliser.Parse`) to a structural allow-list tag (`h1-6`/`heading`/`body`/`list`/`image`); else returns null → the cell renders literally as before. Per `/`-part: heading → bold label; `[Body, bold]` → bold (detected from the bracket text); `[Body]`/`[list]` → plain; `[image]` → `#cellImage`; a text label present ⇒ render the label (bold only in `<td>`, never `<th>`) and DROP decorative images; image-only ⇒ `<img>`. **FREE-BODY ONLY** — a table inside a `cv2-interactive` placeholder shows the raw WT `[tag]` data BY DESIGN, so `insidePlaceholder` skips the inline render (this guard caught a real regression: without it the placeholder tables were stripped, emptying them → body_compare EMPTY-container 87→99 / ANY 128→138; gating to free-body restored 128).
- **Result.** ENGJ402-04 → `<th><b>Line</b></th>`; XGF9003-06 → `<td><b>Organisation</b></td>` (data) + `<th>Executive Function Skill</th>` (header, icon dropped) — matching the human. **Structural-defect audit: literal-`[tag]` leak 883 → 602 occ (−281) / 216 → 183 pages; STRUCTURALLY CLEAN 775 → 807 / 1006 = 77.0 → 80.2%** (beating the round-53 ~730/~79% projection — the lever was bigger than the ~150 estimate). The kept-table structural-leak class is now **0** (re-measured); CEDO501's flip-card FACE tables (widget-member cells = the round-53 class-1 capture lever) are correctly LEFT for that separate build.

**PROTECTED gates (full 197-set + OSSC301 regen, mtime-verified 0 stale / 1006 pages):** compare_structure **4244 → 4249 exact (+5) / 80.0%; EXTRA-container 108 (2.0%) — HELD**; body_compare ANY-breakdown **128 — HELD** (OVER-CAPTURE 39 / RUNAWAY 6 / EMPTY 87); JS regression **REAL FAILURES 0 / HANDLED 100% (9557)**; flipCard **divergence 0** (TOTAL 37: exact 13, copy-edit 10, defect 14); **skeleton SCAFFOLD 46.6%** (pages ≥50% 44.4 → **44.6%**) — HELD-or-improved (the PRIMARY structural gate). A/B (`CELLTAG_OFF`) verified: the toggle cleanly reverts both exemplar cells to the literal-leak form. Per the round-45 rendering-normalisation rule, ships on net match-to-human + protected gates holding (the text-matched WRAP/WIDTH/exact buckets may shift as cleaned cells enter the matched set — expected, not the gate). Data-flagged + env-reversible.

**Remaining levers (sized by round-53 diagnosis, not this round):** the flip-card/face-member raw-table CAPTURE (~475-class, CEDO501 #1) and the free-body widget-member tail (`[tab n]` 223, `[slide]`, `[carousel]` — per-widget capture). Both are fragmented; size by measurement before committing.

The round-50 path-to-semi-working listed "extend the recursive-cell grid to multi-row tables (→ ~86% clean)" as lever 2. I took it on — and the measurement RE-SCOPED it. Even the 11 "content panels" are heterogeneous on inspection: ENGJ402-04 is a poem **rhyme-scheme DATA table** (`[Body, bold]` header row + plain data rows), XGF9003-05 a **skill×level matrix** (`[H2]` first-column label + plain data), XGF9003-02 a **self-assessment checklist** — all of which the human (correctly) keeps as `<table>`. The genuinely grid-able case (XGF9003-04: a 2×4 grid where **every** cell is `[H3] food + image`) is the minority.

"Every cell is a panel" vs "some cells are plain data" is the clean, robust separator (it can't mis-grid a rhyme/ matrix/ checklist table, all of which have plain cells).

Env `LTABLE_OFF` still A/B-reverts the whole grid.

The clean grid subset is small (9 tables). The **bulk of the remaining multi-row leak is WIDGET-DATA tables** — the `[Embedded] [Flipcard]` / `[Item N]` declaration form in ~5 modules, and critically **the top-leak modules PNR101/102/104** — which is a **widget-CAPTURE** fix (read the `[Embedded] [widget]` declaration + the data rows into a built widget), NOT a grid job. ## 2026-06-18 (round 51) — ROW GROUPING: the row-boundary rule MINED from Chris's WT↔human alignment, then SHIPPED (build 260616.30)

Chris proposed anchoring the human's output structure back to the Writers Template to *mine* the boundary rules instead of guessing them — and asked me to evaluate/evolve it, not take it literally. It works; I evolved it into a measurement tool, derived the row-grouping rule, and shipped the fix.

- **`reference/tests/_wt_human_align.py`** — extracts the human's top-level body `div.row`s, anchors each row's first content back to the WT (fuzzy text-match where the content survived rewording; a reworded block just leaves a gap, per Chris's instinct), and reports **which WT tag opens each new human `div.row`**. On OSAI401-01 all 8 rows anchor cleanly (86–100% match): ROW 0 → [Quote] (the whole intro flows into ONE row), ROW 1 → [Activity 1A], ROW 3/5/7 → [H3], ROW 4 → [Activity 1B]. **Corpus (370 pages / 1904 rows): a new div.row opens at a HEADING 24% / ACTIVITY 18% / page-START-quote 14% / CALLOUT 2.4% — and everything else (media, tables, widgets, lists) FLOWS into the current section row** (24% reworded → unanchored, as Chris predicted). This is the **measured** row-grouping rule, the inverse of Claude's "every media/widget gets its own row."
- **The fix (SHIPPED — `data … row_breaks.flow_blocks=true`; `ContentConverter.rowFor` + the new `section` kind on activity/boxed-callout/heading call-sites; env `ROWGROUP_OFF`).** Media/table/widget now FLOW into the current section row; only heading / activity / boxed-callout (`section`) break a row. Two supporting fixes: (a) `emit()` never opens an EMPTY `row>col` (a de-duped lesson-title heading returning `[]` used to leave one); (b) FLOWING callouts (quote/thought) flow into the section row instead of a self-contained box (the page-start quote opens the row and the intro flows in).

**Result + gates (full 197-set regen, 0 stale):** OSAI401-01 top-level body rows **19→12** (human 8) — the intro section (quote + bubble + video + hintSlider + conversations) now flows into ONE row, matching the human. **ROWS RATIO 2.0 → 1.20** (Claude's ~2× row over-emission nearly eliminated — the direct measure of the fix). **PROTECTED: compare_structure 4244 / 80.0% exact + over-nesting 108 — HELD; body_compare 39/6/87/128 — HELD.** tags **100%**; sentinels 4/7/5/7; **0 leaks**; **flipCard 14-baseline HELD**; speechBubble/accordion/clickDrop/tabs verifiers clean. **Skeleton SCAFFOLD match 45.7→46.6%** (pages ≥50%: 41.6→44.4%); the raw scaffold % is capped by the non-derivable column widths (which appear on every line), so it understates the gain — the **width-normalised** OSAI401 row structure is **~56%**. ## 2026-06-18 (round 50) — activity ownership crosses lead headings (2 bugs, 1 fix) + a STRUCTURAL-DEFECT audit & strategy (build 260616.29)

Chris spot-checked OSAI401-01 and flagged two "very basic rule" defects in Activity 1A — plus a deeper question: why do issues keep surfacing despite repeated full-corpus comparisons, and how do we get to a showable semi-working state? Both are addressed.

**The two defects, one root cause.** Activity 1A (a) rendered as `div.activity` WITHOUT the `.interactive` class even though it owns a wordSelect, and (b) over-extended — swallowing the following "People can do…" body + "How AI is used" `<h4>` section + a rotateBanner that belong OUTSIDE. Both stem from one thing: the scanner's **activity-ownership look-back** (which walks from a widget back to its owning `[Activity N]`, crossing the activity's lead content) listed the GENERIC `heading` in `opener_rule.opener_tags`, but the normaliser emits the LEVELLED `h2`-`h5`. So the look-back stopped at Activity 1A's lead `[H4]` "AI Abilities" and never reached `[Activity 1A]` — the wordSelect was never OWNED by 1A, so the activity got no `.interactive` class (it's added when the owned bundle's type ∈ `activity_wrapper.interactive_widget_types`, which includes wordSelect) AND wasn't bounded by the widget. **Fix: add `h2`-`h5` to `opener_tags`** (a one-line data change). Now the wordSelect is owned by 1A → `<div class="activity interactive" number="1A">` AND the activity closes after the widget ("People can do…" / "How AI is used" render outside). Safe: the look-back stops AT the `[activity]` tag, so a section break before the activity is never crossed.

**Result + gates (full 197-set regen, 0 stale):** compare_structure **4212→4244 exact (+32) / over-nesting 108 → 108 — HELD**; body_compare over-capture 39 / runaway 6 — HELD (EMPTY 88→87 / ANY 129→128 — improved); tags **100%**; sentinels 4/7/5/7; **0 leaks**; **flipCard 14-baseline HELD**; speechBubble/accordion/clickDrop/tabs verifiers clean. Structural-defect audit: clean pages **75.0→76.8%**; the `activity-missing-.interactive` defect class **52→25 (halved)**.

**STRATEGIC — why progress felt stuck, and the path forward** (`reference/Why_Progress_Stalls_And_The_Path_Forward.md`; new tools `_structural_defect_audit.py`, `_structural_skeleton.py`, `_skeleton_compare.py`). Chris is right that the spot-check whack-a-mole had to stop, and he had already conceived the fix. Root cause: the element-level discrepancy audit (WRAP 53% / exact 36%) measures only text-MATCHED elements (~30% of a page) and MIXES non-derivable editorial variation with genuine bugs — it cannot answer "is this page structurally correct."

**Two new instruments, the strict text-matched framing demoted:**
- **PRIMARY — simplified-skeleton comparison (Chris's method).** `_structural_skeleton.py` turns a page into a text-stripped structural skeleton (`tag#id.class[attr]`, nesting by indent, repeats collapsed — validated: reproduces Chris's uploaded `OSAI401-01 [simplified html]` line-for-line). `_skeleton_compare.py` scores Claude-vs-human STRUCTURAL MATCH over 100% of the structure, rewording-immune: **RAW 32%** (full structure — low by design, placeholders vs built widgets) and **SCAFFOLD 46%** (widgets collapsed to one `WIDGET` marker — the Phase-1 target). The skeleton DIFF instantly surfaced the **#1 structural lever the aggregate audit never showed: ROW GROUPING** — the human groups a section's content into ONE `row>col`; Claude splits each element into its own row (the "rows ratio 2.0" signal), cascading through every page.
- **COMPANION — structural-defect audit.** `_structural_defect_audit.py` checks rule-based invariants (literal `[tag]` leak / activity `.interactive` / empty activity / raw widget table / sentinel), EXCLUDING by-design placeholders → **% structurally clean = 76.8%** (not 36%). The remaining 23% are dominated by literal `[tag]` leak (1031 occ / 218 pages), 57% inside MULTI-ROW layout tables (Fix 1 deferred).

**Process change (recorded in `reference/Decision_Framework_Human_vs_Claude.md` → MEASUREMENT MANDATE):** judge every structural change FIRST on the skeleton SCAFFOLD match + the % structurally clean, use the per-page skeleton DIFF to find what to fix, and stop treating the text-matched WRAP/WIDTH/exact numbers as correctness. Ranked path to semi-working: (1) ROW GROUPING (raises scaffold match across every page); (2) extend the recursive-cell grid to multi-row tables (→ ~86% clean); (3) non-table literal leaks (→ ~90%+); (4) the small defect tail.

## 2026-06-18 (round 47) — NAMED LEARNING-DESIGN HEADING promotion (the derivable half of TAG h5→p) (build 260616.26)

Fix 2 from the round-46 discrepancy plan, built through the full loop. The Te Kura learning-design headers — **"We are learning to"** (WALT), **"You will show your understanding by"** (WILF), **"Success criteria"**, **"Learning intentions"**, **"How will I know if I've learned it?"** — are a CLOSED, recognisable vocabulary the human developer renders as a HEADING, even when the writer left them as plain untagged text. This is a (B-ii) positional/content convention: derivable from the human's consistent OUTPUT, not the (absent) writer tag.

- **What broke + WT evidence.** AGH1004 WT line 157 `We are learning to ...` is **plain untagged black text** (no `[H5]`) followed by a bulleted intention list → Claude rendered `<p>`. The human renders `<h5>We are learning to:</h5>` inside `#module-menu-content` on every lesson page (AGH1004.01–.09; the .00 overview keeps `<p>`). A GENERIC bold-line→heading rule was correctly declined (round 44 — the same arbitrary phrase splits 2 heading / 14 `<p>` by developer); the NAMED phrases are the derivable subset.
- **Fix (`ContentConverter.#promoteNamedHeadings` + `#widgetRanges`; data `body_region.named_headings`).** A post-pass on the assembled `#body` — run AFTER `#relevelHeadings` so the fixed `h5` survives the rank-normaliser — and on the `#buildMenu` string panes (`tab1/tab2/content/left/right`), since these headers most often live in `#module-menu-content`. A FREE-BODY `<p>` (NOT inside a widget subtree — `#widgetRanges` reuses `heading_relevel.skip_classes`) whose folded text EXACTLY equals a canonical phrase → `<h{level}>` (level 5). The **exact-whole-paragraph** guard (fold strips tags/entities/trailing punctuation, then `===` a phrase) avoids the round-44 false positive — "we are learning about budgeting" ≠ "we are learning to". Env `NAMEDH_OFF` for A/B.
- **Measured net (decisive — matched-pair tag distribution, `outputs/_measure_namedpairs.py`).** Among text-matched pairs where Claude renders the phrase as `<p>`: **WIN 142** (human renders a heading) vs **LOSS 26** (human kept `<p>`) = **NET +116**, of which 128 wins are human=h5 → exact at level 5. Per phrase all positive: "you will show your understanding by" +60, "we are learning to" +30, "success criteria" +23, "learning intentions" +3.

**Result + gates (full 197-set regen, mtime-verified 0 stale):** AGH1004 lesson menus now render `<h5>We are learning to ...</h5>` / `<h5>You will show your understanding by …</h5>`, matching the human. **PROTECTED compare_structure 4143→4146 exact / over-nesting 108 → 108 — HELD; body_compare 39/6/85/127 — HELD** (tag/level never changes the wrapper chain — gate-safe by construction, same property as round 45). tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels 4/7/5/7; **0 leaks**; flipCard 14-baseline + speechBubble/accordion/clickDrop/tabs verifiers clean. **Audit: TAG 10.2%→9.1% (−148), exact 35.3%→35.6% (+40), LEVEL +18** (the lateral cases where the human used h4/h3). A clean net-positive — no trade-off (unlike Fix 1's non-derivable-width dip). Data-flagged + `NAMEDH_OFF` reversible. Tools: `outputs/_measure_named_headings.py`, `_measure_namedpairs.py`.

## 2026-06-18 (round 46) — LAYOUT-TABLE → RECURSIVE-CELL GRID (the round-44 reverted lever, done properly) (build 260616.25)

Round 46 opened with a full corpus-wide Claude-vs-human discrepancy re-survey on the fresh round-45 corpus (`reference/Round46_Discrepancy_Analysis_And_Rectification_Plan.md`: 927 paired pages / 195 modules / 13,783 matched; WRAP 53.4% / WIDTH 28.5% / TAG 10.1% / LEVEL 7.0% / exact 36.0%; gates reproduced after a byte-identical freshness spot-check). The holistic finding: **one mechanism — the writer's layout-table authored as a tagged mini-document per cell — drives a derivable slice of WRAP + WIDTH + TAG at once.** Chris picked it as the build, then approved shipping the measured result.

- **What broke (the bug).** A FREE-BODY content table whose cells embed a `/`-separated tagged mini-document (`[H3]`+`[Image]`+`[Body]`+list, `║`-separated cells; e.g. **CEDO501** "Earned income ║ Unearned income") is a side-by-side LAYOUT the human renders as a `row>col` grid of `<h3>/<img>/<p>/<ul>`. Claude **dumped the literal `[H3]`/`[Image]`/`[Body]` text into a `<th>/<td>`** — not faithful to the writer (the tags are structural directives) and matching no human. Triangulated WT (`…_parsed.txt` line 358) → human gold (`CEDO501_2.0` `row>col-md-4×2`) → Claude (`<th> [H3] Earned income / [Image] … / [Body] …`).
- **Fix (`ContentConverter.#contentTable` → `#layoutTableGrid` / `#renderCellParts` / `#cellImage`; data `body_region.layout_table_grid`).** When `insidePlaceholder===false` (free-body tables only — placeholder/widget tables stay raw so their captured data is visible) and the table is **SINGLE-ROW** (a 1-row table is never an MCQ/comparison DATA table) and a cell carries a recognised structural `[tag]` and **no** cell carries a widget-member tag (`#norm.GetWidgetTypes` guard → a mis-captured flipCard/carousel stays raw), each cell is rendered as a `col`: split `║`→cells, `/`→parts, run each `[tag]` part back through the element renderer (heading→`<hN>` at the writer digit+`body_shift`, re-leveller then normalises; `[image]`→the image emitter; body/bullets→`#renderBlackText`→`<p>`/`<ul>`). Col width derived from the cell COUNT (2→col-md-6, 3→col-md-4, 4→col-md-3). At the body top level the grid is emitted as its **own** `row` (no `col-md-8` wrapper) to match the human's bare `row>col`. Genuine data tables (no structural `[tag]`) keep the raw `<table>`. **Conservative scope (single-row only):** multi-row tagged tables (91 corpus-wide) deferred — a multi-row tagged table may be a per-row panel set OR a data table with a tagged header row, which needs its own measurement.
- **Cross-cutting / measured class.** 838 tables / 2,917 literal-`[tag]` cells in 89 modules carry the bug overall; the clean built slice = **125 single-row multi-cell + 23 single-cell free-body tagged tables across ~35 modules / 729 cells**, spanning CEDO/CEDR/CEDW, ENGC/ENGI/ENGR/ENGS, MXFU, PNR, OSAI/OSBY/OSGM/OSOH, XGF, XTAS — the `/`-separated tagged mini-document is a cross-family authoring form.

**Result + gates (full 197-set regen, mtime-verified 0 stale; 729 literal-`[tag]` cells fixed):** CEDO501-02 now renders `row>col-md-6 > h3+img+p+ul` ×2 (the "earned income" cell lands at `h3 @ row>col` — **TAG + wrapper chain now MATCH the human**; only the non-derivable col width differs). **PROTECTED body_compare 42/6/85/130 → 39/6/85/127 — IMPROVED.** **PROTECTED compare_structure over-nesting 108 → 108 — HELD;** exact-chain **4070 → 4143 (+73 abs)** (rate 80.6%→79.9% = denominator growth: the grid surfaces ~134 previously-unmatchable cells, 54% chain-exact). tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7; **0 sentinel leaks**; flipCard 14-baseline held; speechBubble / accordion / clickDrop verifiers **0 defects**.

**The honest trade-off (shipped on net match-to-human + protected gates holding — Chris's call).** The content-paired audit ticks DOWN — **exact 36.0→35.3% (−35), WIDTH 28.5→29.5% (+197), WRAP 53.4→54.0% (+203), matched 13,783→13,986 (+203)** — because the fix moves the cells INTO the matched set, where they match tag+text+chain but mismatch the **non-derivable column width** (measured: human 2-col panels are none 43% / col-md-8 21% / col-md-4 17% / col-md-6 10% — no derivable majority). The audit exact% structurally cannot credit this fix — the only way to avoid the WIDTH penalty is to keep the bug. Judged on the corrected output (729 cells now render the human's actual structure vs literal `[tag]` junk) + the improved protected body gate + held over-nesting, per the round-45 rule that rendering normalisations ship on net match-to-human. Data-flagged + `LTABLE_OFF` env A/B for reversal. Tools: `outputs/_probe_celltable.cjs`, `_measure_layouttable.py`, `_measure_freebodytable.py`, `_measure_tablerows.py`, `_measure_panelwidth.py`.

## 2026-06-18 (round 45) — DOCUMENT-LEVEL heading re-levelling (Chris's holistic hypothesis, confirmed) + 4 loosened rules (build 260616.24)

Chris's insight: my round-44 "LEVEL is non-derivable" verdict came from a PER-TAG measurement (writer digit → human level), which structurally can't see document-level logic. He hypothesised the human developers follow a consistent heading hierarchy across the whole page even though the per-tag mapping looks random. **Measured the human heading SCAFFOLDING (ignoring content) and he was right:**

- **71% of human pages start their body at `h3`**; body headings collapse to a clean `h3 > h4 > h5` outline; 73% of pages are well-formed (no skip-down >1). The human **ignores the writer's `[H?]` digit** and re-bases every page to an h3-top hierarchy.
- The writer's tag is noise; the human's consistent OUTPUT convention is the signal — invisible per-tag, clear per-document.

- **Fix — `ContentConverter.#relevelHeadings`, a post-pass on the assembled `#body`.** The page's DISTINCT free-body heading levels (sorted) map to `h3, h4, h5, …` (a rank normalisation, clamped at `max_level`). Data: `Emit_Templates.body_region.heading_relevel` (`enabled`/`base_level`/`max_level`/`skip_classes`); env `RELEVEL_OFF` for A/B. Measured: writer+1 **46.2% → rank 57.5%** match on text-matched body headings.
- **Scope / safety.** Only FREE-BODY headings — headings inside a widget subtree (`skip_classes`: the `cv2-interactive` placeholder + every built-widget class) are left untouched, so the widget verifiers and the widgets' own heading conventions are protected. A two-pass tag-walk tracks div nesting to know which headings are inside a widget. **GATE-SAFE by construction**: heading level never changes the row/col/activity wrapper chain.

**Result + gates (full 197-set regen, mtime-verified 0 stale):** **compare_structure 4070 / 80.6% / over-nesting 108 (2.1%) / missing 161 (3.2%) — IDENTICAL**; **body_compare 42 / 6 / 85 / 130 — IDENTICAL**; tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7; **0 sentinel leaks**; flipCard 14-baseline + speechBubble / accordion / clickDrop verifiers clean. **Audit LEVEL 8.5% → 7.0% (−213 heading-level mismatches fixed), exact 35.7% → 36.0%.** A/B (RELEVEL_OFF vs ON) on a 6-module sample: heading-level mismatches **76 → 44**. AGH1004 page 5.0: its 6 section headings flip h4 → h3, matching the human.

**Also this round — process (Chris's standing mandates):**
- **WT-VISIBILITY MANDATE (round 44, baked in):** every detected issue / proposed fix MUST SHOW the raw writers-template structure + full context, side-by-side with human + Claude — never an abstract description. In the kickoff (loop step a) + `reference/Decision_Framework_Human_vs_Claude.md`.
- **4 LOOSENED RULES (round 45, baked in)** — the strictness was hiding real wins: (1) analyze HOLISTICALLY / document-level before declaring "non-derivable"; (2) "derivable" includes the human's OUTPUT conventions, not just the WT tag; (3) NET-POSITIVE replaces zero-regression for the finer audit buckets (protected gates still hold); (4) "never half-build" is for widget BUILDS, not rendering NORMALISATIONS (which ship on net match-to-human). In the kickoff §3 + the Decision Framework.

## 2026-06-18 (round 44) — the 197-set's three top-discrepancy levers MEASURED & TESTED; none ships (no engine change; build stays 260616.23)

Also this round: reconciled `01-Claude_Modules_` to Chris's signed-off **197-module list** (converted 91 missing, deleted 89 out-of-list; `batch_convert` now defaults to `compare_set.txt`); fixed the audit's page-pairing to be **content-based** (the human sub-paginates `0.0,0.1,…` while Claude numbers `00,01,…` — numeric pairing dropped/mis-paired ~25 modules); and re-ran the full survey on the 197-set (`reference/Compare_Set_197_Discrepancy_Survey.md`: WRAP 53.4% / WIDTH 28.5% / TAG 10.1% / LEVEL 8.5%, exact 35.7% — harder than the old set). Then worked the survey's three "actionable" levers through the loop — **all three declined/reverted with evidence** (`reference/Round44_Three_Levers_Measured.md`):

- **LEVEL `body_shift` 0 vs +1 — no change.** Measured: +1 hits 46.2% of matched body headings vs 41.2% for 0; switching to 0 fixes ~817 too-deep headings but breaks ~918 exact ones (net −101). The heading drift is per-instance editorial re-levelling, not a global-shift bug. **+1 is optimal.**

Blanket promotion is ~54% precise (breaks 70 to fix 96). No text feature discriminates. **Declined.**
- **Layout-table → grid — implemented, A/B-tested, reverted.** The conservative single-row unpacker (data-flagged + `UNPACK_OFF` toggle) was **structure/body-gate-neutral** (table cells are unmatched short labels) but **worsened the rows ratio 1.60→1.70** and **garbled output** — the single-row "layout" tables embed a rich tagged sub-layout per cell (`[H3]`+`[Image]`+`[Body]`+list, e.g. CEDO501's income panels) that the naive unpack dumps as literal text. **Reverted.** The proper fix parses each cell as a sub-document (recursive cell rendering) — the substantial layout-table build the survey predicted, now precisely scoped as the highest-value real next build.

**Net:** the loop prevented three bad changes; the corpus is at the round-43 baseline (compare_structure 80.6% / over-nesting 2.1% / missing 3.2%; tags 100%; 0 sentinel leaks; gates confirmed unchanged after reverting the lever-1 test regens).

## 2026-06-17 (round 43) — instruction RETENTION: embedded CS:/Dev:/Note: notes are surfaced as red text after the widget, not discarded (build 260616.23)

Two-part round. **(1)** A full-corpus Claude-vs-human discrepancy survey (all 1011 paired pages / 193 modules, on a fully-regenerated corpus — `reference/Round43_Full_Corpus_Discrepancy_Survey.md`), which also found + fixed a **page-pairing bug** in `full_compare.py` (dot-named human files never paired → 39 modules silently dropped; corrected in the new `_discrepancy_audit.py`). **(2)** Worked the #1 discrepancy class (WRAP, 49%) through the loop: triangulation + measurement showed it is mostly **non-derivable layout variation + faithful-to-writer editorial divergence** (recorded in `reference/Round43_WRAP_Diagnosis.md`). Chris then relaxed two project rules and supplied a standing **decision framework** (recorded in `reference/Decision_Framework_Human_vs_Claude.md`): match the human when there's a tag-link or a positional/content convention; ignore true uncatalogable editorial; and — the concrete fix this round — **never silently strip a documented instruction; retain it as red text after its element.**

- **What broke (the round-42 over-correction).** Round 42 made a speechBubble build by `#stripDevSpans`-ing a `🔴[RED TEXT] [CS: …] [/RED TEXT]🔴` developer note out of the cell — but it **discarded** the note. Chris's rule: a documented instruction (the `Instruction_Cues.json` vocab — cs/csc/dev/developer/note/please/can you…) is written by the writer to guide the human designer of v1; it must be **kept and shown**, as red paragraph text, **immediately after the element it was attached to** (or at the **bottom but inside** the activity container if the element lives in one). The human gold never shows these (they're v1 dialogue, stripped by the designer), so this is Claude surfacing something the human doesn't — by design.
- **Fix (`ContentConverter`, shared + capture-neutral).** New `#bundleInstructions(bundle)` harvests every red span the **normaliser** classifies as an instruction (`parse.class === "instruction"`/`instructionFragment`) from the bundle's `tables` cells, `memberItems`, `openerItems`, plus the scanner's standalone `bundle.instructions`, deduped. `#interactivePlaceholder` now emits these as red `<p>` (the existing `#redFlag` form) **after a BUILT widget** — previously only the placeholder path surfaced standalone instructions, so a built widget dropped them. Placement falls out of the existing emission order: for an activity-owned widget the return value is emitted before the activity close → bottom-but-inside the activity; for an inline widget → right after it. The round-42 strip stays (keeps the BUILD clean); this only re-surfaces what it dropped. **Generalised across EVERY interactive** (the cross-cutting mandate), not just speechBubble — it reads the bundle, never a per-widget method.
- **Why safe (capture-neutral).** `#bundleInstructions` only READS the bundle and appends Claude-only red `<p>`s after the widget subtree (which the gates exclude on both sides), so no wrapper chain, free-body range, or widget build changes.

**Result + gates (full 195-module regen, mtime-verified 0 stale; 10 modules / 13 pages changed):** OSAI201 now shows `RED FLAG: CS: can a cross be put through the brain image…` after the Aria bubble; HES1007 "Designer: please add as image…", XMES103 "Note to Dev team…", XGF9001 "[Note for Creative Services…]", MXDB302 flipCard content notes, OSAI101 "CS can these pieces be separated…" all surfaced. **compare_structure 4943 exact / 87.5% / 102 over-nesting (1.8%) / 220 missing — IDENTICAL**; **body_compare 43 / 4 / 65 / 112 — IDENTICAL**; tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7; **0 sentinel leaks**; **speechBubble verifier 0 defects**, **flipCard 14-defect baseline held**, accordion / clickDrop / tabs verifiers clean.

## 2026-06-17 (round 42) — speech bubbles: a "CS:" note / "flipside:" reveal no longer blocks the build (build 260616.22)

Chris flagged broken speech bubbles on OSAI201-01. Triangulated (`_probe_bundle.cjs` + WT lines 84/224 + the human OSAI201-01.html):

- **#1 (Aria) — a CS note in the image cell.** WT: `[speech bubble] Kia ora! I'm Ariā… ║ [image] <iStock url> / 🔴[CS: can a cross be put through the brain image to show it is AI is not a brain.]🔴`. The "CS:" developer note is a SECOND red span in the image cell, so the round-11/31 `#redSpanCount > 1` guard bailed. But the human BUILDS the bubble — the CS note is a MANUAL image edit (put a cross through the brain), not bubble content.
- **#8 (Generative AI) — a "flipside:" reveal in the text cell.** WT: `[image] <url> ║ [speech bubble] Generative AI is a type of computer program… conversations. / 🔴[flipside:]🔴 When asked or prompted, it learns…`. The "flipside:" is a SECOND red span → bail. The human renders BOTH parts as the bubble's paragraphs.
- **Fix (`InteractiveBuilder`, conservative + data-driven).** New `#stripDevSpans(cell, prefixes)` drops red spans whose content starts (at a word boundary) with a droppable prefix — `cs` / `dev` / `note` (a developer MANUAL-edit instruction → not content) or `flipside` / `flip side` (a reveal LABEL → the text after it is the bubble's second part) — KEEPING the surrounding learner text and the widget's own `[image]`/`[speech bubble]` tag span. `#speechBubble` applies it to BOTH cells before the `#redSpanCount`/residual guards; the image residual also dissolves the "/" the writer left before a removed CS note. So: #1 builds (CS note dropped, the bubble keeps just its text + the iStock image — the developer adds the cross-through-brain asset by hand, per the note in the manifest); #8 builds with both paragraphs (the surviving " / " feeds the round-34 multi-paragraph path). Any OTHER unrecognised 2nd red span STILL bails (conservative). Prefixes are data-tunable: `Emit_Templates.interactive_builders.speechBubble.droppable_span_prefixes`.
- **Measured class:** 7 modules carry a speech-bubble CS-note/flipside (ANZH205, ENGS101, OSAI101, OSAI201, OSGM101, OSSC301, TEFUN01). The fix is faithful — the speechBubble verifier classes every new build against the human gold.

**Result + gates (7 affected modules regenerated, mtime-verified):** OSAI201 now builds #1 + #8 (the CS note dropped — 0 inline leak — and the flipside as a 2-paragraph bubble); OSAI101/OSGM101/OSSC301 gain bubbles too. **compare_structure 4907 → 4931 exact (+24) / 87.5% / 102 over-nesting (1.8%) — IMPROVED** (each built bubble replaces a mismatching orange placeholder + its content); **body_compare 42 / 4 / 65 / 111 — HELD**; tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7; **flipCard A/B BYTE-IDENTICAL**; **`_verify_speechbubble.cjs` 0 defects** across all affected + canonical modules. (#7 on the same page still correctly bails — its image cell has no derivable iStock URL, a different/legitimate reason.)

## 2026-06-17 (round 41) — inline infoTrigger: the NON-BOLD anchor (build 260616.21)

Round 40 built the infoTrigger span only when the anchor was a clear **bold/italic** run. But the anchor is bolded only ~20% of the time — measured across the human corpus, **81% of the 1,603 infoTrigger anchors are a SINGLE word** ("contempt", "whānau", "kōrero", "onomatopoeia", "stanzas", "decisions"…), 16% two words, 3% three. So a non-bold anchor previously dropped the definition (plain text). This round builds them.

- **Fix (`ContentConverter.#inlineMarkup`).** After the bold/italic infoTrigger rule, a second rule wraps the single WORD immediately before the sentinel: `(word)<sentinel>DEF</sentinel>` → `<span class="infoTrigger" info="DEF">word</span>`. Word chars include macrons/diacritics, digits, hyphens, apostrophes; a leading non-letter (e.g. a writer `✅` marker) is left OUTSIDE the span. A multi-word non-bold anchor gets its LAST word wrapped — the definition stays correct on a partial anchor (still far better than dropping it); the bold path already covers the bolded multi-word terms.
- **Fix (`InteractiveScanner` re-stitch) — recover the in-marker anchor.** Some writers put the anchor term INSIDE the marker bracket, before the sub-tag: SSFUN07 "…or become 🔴[ obsolete [rollover definition: 🔴 no longer in use 🔴] ]🔴?" — the marker's own text is "obsolete [rollover definition:". The old code dropped that leading "obsolete" (so it was LOST from the page AND my first non-bold pass mis-wrapped the preceding word "become"). The re-stitch now lifts the leading term (the part of the marker text before the first "[") out and places it right before the sentinel, so it is kept AND becomes the wrapped anchor: "become <span class=\"infoTrigger\" info=\"no longer in use\">obsolete</span>". (ENGC201's "[hovertrigger:" has no leading term → "" → the anchor stays the preceding black word.)
- **Result:** infoTrigger spans **20 → 31** (the 11 new ones are non-bold anchors: ENGC201 contempt, SSFUN07 obsolete/consumers/excessive, BLL252 fiction/onomatopoeia/poet, …), **0 sentinel leaks** corpus-wide. Spans are inline within their `<p>`, so they don't change wrapper chains (gate-invisible) but add the human's hover.

**Gates (28 infoTrigger compare-set modules regenerated, mtime-verified):** **compare_structure 4907 exact / 87.5% / 102 (1.8%) — HELD** (the inline spans don't alter `<p>`/`<li>` chains); **body_compare 42 / 4 / 65 / 111 — HELD**; tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7; **flipCard A/B BYTE-IDENTICAL**.

**Still open (smaller, recorded):** a non-separate-closer marker shape — ENGI203 "**fake news** [hover trigger – def]" where the `]` and DEF share one red span (no standalone `]` item) — doesn't re-stitch yet, so it renders `<b>fake news</b>` without the hover (the bold is kept; not a leak). A multi-word non-bold anchor still wraps only its last word.

## 2026-06-17 (round 40) — inline infoTrigger BUILT (the `[hovertrigger: DEF]` paragraph-split + definition-leak, fixed) (build 260616.20)

The deferred Workstream B from rounds 37/39. A writer drops a hover/rollover definition INLINE as `term [hovertrigger: DEFINITION] continuation` (ENGC201-00 "This **whakatauki** [hovertrigger: Proverb] reinforces…"; -01 "[alert] The **universal expressions** [hover-trigger: Expressions…] are believed to be:"; -02 "We avoid using **contractions** [hover-trigger: Short forms of words.] in formal situations."). 

- **Why it broke (triangulated with `_probe_infotrigger.cjs`).** The parser splits that one inline construct into THREE items: the preceding ANCHOR item, the marker (its `blackAfter` = the DEFINITION), and a `]` CLOSER item (`primary=null`, its `blackAfter` = the rest of the sentence). The old standalone-marker handling re-exposed the marker's `blackAfter` (the DEFINITION) as body text — a LEAK — and the `]` closer rendered its continuation as a SEPARATE `<p>` — a SPLIT. Result: "This whakatauki" / "Proverb" / "reinforces…" as three paragraphs (and in the alert, the definition leaked inline and the list spilled out).
- **Fix — re-stitch + build the span.** `InteractiveScanner` (standalone-marker handling): for an infoTrigger marker FOLLOWED by a `]` closer, drop the definition onto the anchor as an inline annotation (encoded in a private-use sentinel U+E000…U+E001 right after the anchor) and re-join the continuation, so the whole construct is ONE item/paragraph; the `]` closer is consumed. `ContentConverter.#inlineMarkup`: after the `**bold**`/`*italic*` pass, wrap the IMMEDIATELY-preceding bold/italic run in `<span class="infoTrigger" info="DEF">` (data template `inline_format.info_trigger`); the DEF is already HTML-escaped → attribute-safe. The sentinel **never appears in ordinary text**, so non-infoTrigger lines are byte-untouched.
- **Conservative where the anchor isn't derivable.** The human anchors the span on the preceding word(s), bolded only ~20% of the time. Building reliably needs a clear anchor, so the span is built ONLY when the anchor is a trailing **bold/italic** run (the dominant flagged form); a plain unbolded anchor (e.g. the list item "contempt") drops the sentinel → plain text, the definition deferred (NEVER a leaked inline string). A BARE standalone marker with no `]` closer keeps the round-19/20 page-swallow guard. So every case is either built correctly or rendered as correct plain text — never the old split/leak.
- **Result:** ENGC201-00 → `<p>This <span class="infoTrigger" info="Proverb">whakatauki</span> reinforces…</p>` (one paragraph, matching the human); -01 alert → `<p>The <span class="infoTrigger" info="Expressions that are the same around the world.">universal expressions</span> are believed to be:</p>` INSIDE the box, the definition only in the `info=` attribute; -02 contractions likewise. **20 spans built across 15 modules**, **0 sentinel leaks** corpus-wide.

**Gates (28 infoTrigger compare-set modules regenerated, mtime-verified complete):** **compare_structure 4900 → 4907 exact (+7) / 87.5% / 102 over-nesting (1.8%) — IMPROVED** (the re-stitched single paragraphs now match the human's single `<p>`); **body_compare 42 / 4 / 65 / 111 — HELD**; tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7; **flipCard A/B BYTE-IDENTICAL** (the sentinel rules only fire on sentinel-bearing text; table-cell markup is untouched); speechBubble + accordion verifiers clean (incl. SSFUN07, an infoTrigger module). 

**Still open (separate, smaller):** the non-bold anchor span (build on the preceding word when not bolded — needs an anchor-span measurement); the un-bulleted emotion list in ENGC201-01's alert (the items are plain lines in the WT, not a `[list]`, so rendering them as `<p>` is faithful — a `<ul>` would be guessing); empty-box causes 2a `[Interactive]`-alias + 2b ownership-walkback.

## 2026-06-17 (round 39) — consecutive activity openers collapse into ONE box + a stale-regen discovery & clean re-baseline (build 260616.19)

Two parallel asks from Chris: (A) the remaining empty activity boxes (HIS1008 / HIS1007 / ANZH401), and (B) the inline-infoTrigger build. Investigated both with parallel triangulation agents.

### (A) Consecutive activity openers — FIXED
- **Cause (the dominant ~69% of remaining empty boxes).** Writers pair a layout/mode NOTE tag with the real numbered tag: HIS-style `[Activity Individual]` (or `[Activity Interactive]`, `[Activity individual – full width of the page]`) then `[Activity 1A] …`; or the inverse CEDK-style `[Activity 1B]` then `[Activity body] …`. ALL canonicalise to tag `activity` (CONTAINER_OPEN), so the first opens a box and the second immediately auto-closes it EMPTY (CONTAINER_OPEN is a close-before directive), spilling the content.
- **Fix (`ContentConverter` activity dispatch).** When an `[activity]` opener has NO content of its own AND the next non-blank item is ALSO an `[activity]` opener, SUPPRESS the (note) half — the other opener makes the box; the activity NUMBER is carried to whichever opener lacks it (so the box stays numbered, e.g. CEDK's `[Activity 1B]` number flows onto `[Activity body]`). Robust to either order and to the layout-word spelling.
- **Result:** empty activity boxes **91 → 31** (clean). HIS1008 27→0, HIS1007 17→0, ANZH303 8→0, ANZH203 3→0, etc. Fired on exactly 7 modules; **gate-NEUTRAL** (see below).
- **Remaining (deferred, measured):** 31 boxes from two OTHER causes — 2a `[Interactive]` instruction-alias opening a box whose only content is a writer note (ANZH401, 14), and 2b the scanner activity-ownership walk-back stopping on `h2`/`h3` (the bank's `opener_tags` lists `"heading"` but the normaliser emits `"h2"`/`"h3"`) so the widget renders inline and the box empties (AGH1009, 7). Both are clean, separable next steps.

### (B) inline infoTrigger build — DEFERRED to its own round (with Chris's agreement)
Triangulation (agent + `_probe_infotrigger.cjs`) showed it is much larger than the "anchor = preceding bold" rule I proposed: the anchor is the preceding **bold** run only **~20%** of the time (the true anchor is the preceding word(s), usually UNbolded — 1,645 human inline spans); the definition payload sits in **three** different places (colon-in-bracket → `remainders`, `blackAfter` up to the `]` closer, or a following item); **~24%** are payload-less `[rollover definition]` markers that MUST stay dropped; and the split+leak needs a cross-item re-stitch (the `]`-closer item carries the post-marker sentence and also breaks the ENGC201-01 alert's strict gather). Reach: **~132 modules / 874 markers**. A 132-module inline-rendering change must be measured & proven on its own, not rushed. Full design recorded in `reference/Menu_And_InlineInfoTrigger_Findings.md`; probe `reference/tests/_probe_infotrigger.cjs` kept.

### ⚠️ Process discovery — stale regens (corrected this round)
While re-measuring, found that the earlier batch regens (rounds 36-38, 32-module batches) had been **silently timing out at the 44 s sandbox limit and leaving the tail of each batch un-regenerated** — so most `01-Claude_Modules_/` files were stale (Jun-16 / round-35), and the rounds 36-38 corpus gate %s were measured on stale/mixed files. The per-module fixes were each verified correct individually, but the corpus numbers were not trustworthy. **Corrected:** did a clean COMPLETE regen in smaller batches WITH a per-module mtime completeness check (re-running stragglers until 0 stale, except 4 `X*` extras not in batch_convert's representative/holdout lists — constant across all rounds). 

**New CLEAN baselines (the first trustworthy ones in several rounds):** compare_structure **4900 exact / 87.5% / 102 over-nesting (1.8%) / 0 errors**; body_compare **42 / 4 / 65 / 111**; tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7; flipCard A/B byte-identical. The body over-capture **42** (not the previously-documented "37") is the TRUE clean number — the 37 was a stale-file artifact, NOT a regression. **Workstream A proven gate-neutral by an explicit on/off A/B** (regen the 7 affected modules with the rule disabled vs enabled): structure 4900/87.5%/102 and body 42/4/65/111 were **byte-identical** both ways; only the empty-box count moved (91→31).

## 2026-06-17 (round 38) — ENGC201-01: an activity's own title heading no longer auto-closes the box EMPTY (build 260616.18)

Chris flagged ENGC201-01 Activity **1B "Creating emotion avatars"**: the box rendered EMPTY and all its content (heading, image, numbered list, "Video instructions", the video, the Avatar-maker / journal links) spilled OUTSIDE, below the box. Triangulated WT→human→Claude.

- **WT (lines 204-228):** `[Activity 1B]` (split across red spans) → `[Activity heading H3] Creating emotion avatars` → `[side image]` → `[body]` → numbered list → `[H5] Video instructions` → `[body]` → `[video]` → `[external link]` → `[link to journal]` → `[End page]`. The activity owns **no interactive widget** (video / external-link / button are ELEMENTs), so it is a PLAIN activity container, NOT the round-33 owns-a-widget path (which is why sibling 1A — which owns a carousel — rendered correctly).
- **Root cause (`ContentConverter.ConvertPage#autoClose`):** an open activity auto-closes before any heading rendered at level ≤ `rendered_heading_max` (3) — UNCONDITIONALLY. So `[Activity 1B]` opened, then its OWN `[Activity heading H3]` (rendered level 3) immediately tripped autoClose → the activity closed EMPTY and its title + content rendered as free body outside. (The `heading_closes_after_first_content` guard existed only in the SUPERSEDED callout block, never for activities.)
- **Human:** the 1B box CONTAINS its title + all the content (the human nests it `activity > … > content`).
- **Robust fix (data + `#autoClose`):** an activity's OWN TITLE heading belongs INSIDE and must not close the box. (a) an `[activity heading]` is ALWAYS the title (`activity_close_before.title_heading_tags`) → never closes; (b) a plain section heading (H2-H5 ≤ `rendered_heading_max`) is the activity's title when it is the FIRST thing after the `[Activity N]` opener (before any content) → stays inside; only AFTER the activity has content is such a heading a section break that closes it (`heading_closes_only_after_content`). An explicit `[end activity]` / a new `[Activity]` / a section marker / a page boundary still close it exactly as before. Robust to the writer using either `[Activity heading]` OR a plain `[H3]` for the title, and to the split-tag spelling.
- **Measured class:** the empty-activity-box spill = **246 boxes across 59 modules** before; **190 / 36 after** — this fix corrects **56 boxes** (the title-heading subset, incl. ENGC201-01 1B). The remaining 190 are OTHER causes (concentrated in HIS1008 27 / HIS1007 17 / ANZH401 14) — a separate class to measure next.

**Result + gates (full 194-module compare-set regenerated):** **compare_structure exact RATE held at 87.5% / over-nesting held at 102 (1.8%) / 0 comparator errors** — the absolute exact count 4931→4911 (−20) is a DENOMINATOR shrink, not a structural regression: total claude content elements dropped 20091→19865 (−226) as content merges into activity wrappers, text-matched 5633→5613 (−20), and the −20 lost-exact elements simply left the matched set with **ZERO movement to a worse bucket** (diff-order 328 / EXTRA 102 / missing 219 all unchanged). **body_compare 40 / 4 / 63 / 107** — the over-capture +3 (and ANY +3) is the **documented free-body-shrink artifact** (rounds 20/22/28): correctly nesting activity content shrinks Claude's free-body, so a pre-existing UN-built widget on the same page crosses the 40% line — the widget bundles (scanner ranges) are unchanged, so this is not new breakage. tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7; **flipCard A/B BYTE-IDENTICAL** (the change is in `#autoClose`, widget-builder-neutral); accordion / speechBubble verifiers clean.

## 2026-06-17 (round 37) — BLL252-00: module-menu bullets now group into one `<ul>`; ENGC201 inline-infoTrigger + untagged whakataukī diagnosed (build 260616.17)

Chris flagged three items across BLL252 + ENGC201; triangulated each WT→human→Claude.

1. **BLL252-00 `#module-menu-content` lists not grouped — FIXED.** The overview menu's Knowledge / Practices / Learning Intentions / Success Criteria are `•`-bulleted lists; the human renders each as ONE tight `<ul>`, but Claude emitted a SEPARATE one-`<li>` `<ul>` per bullet (≈30 `<ul>`s, with big vertical gaps). **Root cause:** the menu items are partitioned out of the stream BEFORE `#coalesceBlackRuns` runs (that's why FREE-BODY bullets already group — they're coalesced — but MENU bullets don't), and `#buildMenu` rendered each black item/line through its own `#renderBlackText` call → a one-item list each. The Blended-Literacy two-column (`two_col_li`) form renders per-LINE, so it splits even within a single item. **Robust fix (`ContentConverter.#buildMenu`):** BUFFER consecutive black content and flush it as ONE `#renderBlackText` block — before any heading / table / column (bucket) switch / consumed section-label, and once at the end. This covers every archetype (tabs / flat / two_col_li). Paragraph-safe: `#renderBlackText` re-splits on newlines, so non-bullet paragraphs still emit as separate `<p>`; only consecutive bullets group. Mirrors the round-35 activity-lead buffering, now for the menu. BLL252-00 menu: ≈30 one-item `<ul>` → **5 grouped `<ul>`**, matching the human. (Known residual, NOT this fix: the `*`-prefixed SUB-bullets under "Decoding an unknown word involves:" still render as `<p>*…` — the human nests them in a child `<ul>`; recognising `* ` as a bullet conflicts with `*italic*` markdown, so it needs its own measured pass.)

2. **ENGC201-00 whakataukī — diagnosed; split into a derivable part (deferred to a measured round) + a non-derivable part (recorded).** WT line 112: `This **whakatauki** [hovertrigger: Proverb] reinforces the importance…`. The human renders ONE flowing `<p>`: `This <span class="infoTrigger" info="Proverb">whakatauki</span> reinforces…`. Claude SPLIT it into three paragraphs — "This whakatauki" / "Proverb" / "reinforces…" — because the inline `[hovertrigger: <def>]` marker fragments the line (`[trigger:` + `<def>` + `]` are separate red spans) and the standalone-inline-marker handling RE-EXPOSES the marker's payload (the definition "Proverb") as body text instead of dropping it, while the surrounding fragments stay as separate items. **The derivable rule (next round):** an inline `[infotrigger/hovertrigger/rollover: DEFINITION]` annotates the immediately-preceding **bold** run — render `<span class="infoTrigger" info="DEFINITION">BOLD</span>` inline and keep the paragraph whole (and the conservative fallback is the same minus the span: drop the definition, re-join the text). **Non-derivable part (recorded):** the proverb + translation BOX (`<div class="whakatauki">`) — the WT has NO `[whakataukī]` tag here (lines 108/110 are plain italic text); the human developer recognised the bilingual proverb and boxed it. Building it would mean guessing a whakataukī from untagged italics → declined (never guess).

3. **ENGC201-01 "universal expressions" alert box — same inline-infoTrigger root.** WT line 148: `[alert] The **universal expressions** [hover-trigger: Expressions that are the same around the world.] are believed to be:` + a bulleted list. The human renders the box holding `<p>The <span class="infoTrigger" info="…">universal expressions</span> are believed to be:</p>` + a grouped `<ul>`. Claude leaked the definition inline (": Expressions that are the same around the world.") and pushed "are believed to be:" + the (ungrouped) list OUTSIDE the box. Same fix family as #2 (the inline-infoTrigger handling) plus the alert-callout-holds-the-list boundary — scoped with #2 for the next round.

**Measurement (scoping #2/#3):** the inline `[…trigger: definition]` pattern = **190 occurrences across 18 modules** (a bounded class; infoTrigger is ~1,669 inline spans corpus-wide, so the inline build is broad and merits its own measured pass to avoid regressions — not rushed into this round).

**Result + gates (full 194-module compare-set regenerated):** the menu fix is **structurally NEUTRAL** (grouping bullets changes the number of `<ul>` parents but not any `<li>`'s wrapper CHAIN, which is what `compare_structure` measures, and the menu is in `#header` not `#body`): **compare_structure 4931 exact (87.5%) / 102 over-nesting (1.8%) — HELD**; **body_compare 37 / 4 / 63 / 104 — HELD**; tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7; **flipCard A/B BYTE-IDENTICAL** (the change is in `#buildMenu`, widget-neutral); accordion / speechBubble verifiers clean. ## 2026-06-16 (round 36) — XGF9001-00: accordion inline-marker member + speechBubble self-captioned over-capture (build 260616.16)

Chris flagged two XGF9001-00 (overview) defects; triangulated each WT→human→Claude (`_probe_bundle.cjs` + the parsed WT + the human gold), then fixed the CLASS, measured corpus-wide.

1. **Accordion not built — an inline `[highlight text]` member dropped MID-PARAGRAPH.** WT line: `[Accordion 1] [H3] Te ao Māori. [Body] In te ao Māori… Māori perspectives value [highlight text] **mana…(creative expression)** as key aspects… honouring whakapapa… as **taonga (treasures)** to be nurtured and shared.` The writer placed a `[highlight text]` (→ wordSelect) INLINE inside the panel body; the parser split that ONE paragraph into a `[body]` member ("…value") + a `[word select]` member (the rest of the paragraph). `#accordionTextOnly` hit the `[word select]` tag at case (c) "anything else → bail," so the whole accordion stayed an orange placeholder. The human renders the panel as ONE `<p>` (the highlighted phrase as `<span class="highlight">`). **Robust fix (`InteractiveBuilder`, builder-only):** the member-text builders — `#accordionTextOnly`, `#accordionWithImages`, `#tabs`, `#clickDrop` — now treat an INLINE-MARKER member as body CONTINUATION of the current panel/item, merging its text into the last paragraph (shared `#isInlineMarkerMember` + `#mergeBodyContinuation`). The marker set is data-first: a member whose lexicon `widget_types` intersect `member_rule.{inline_markers, standalone_inline_markers}` (wordSelect/wordHighlighter/infoTrigger) — so any future highlight/rollover alias is covered. The highlight/tooltip STYLING is non-derivable, so Phase-1 renders the annotated text as readable plain text (the inline-marker policy); the writer's `**bold**` still becomes `<b>`. **Safe by construction:** a clean build has no inline-marker members, so no currently-building widget changes (flipCard A/B byte-identical; accordion/clickDrop/tabs plain forms unchanged). **Measured:** 14 widgets — 7 accordion / 5 clickDrop / 2 tabs across 7 modules — were bailing purely on this. XGF9001 now builds its overview accordion (Te ao Māori / Pasifika cultures) + a page-2 clickDrop, all faithful (0 defects).

2. **speechBubble over-capture — a SELF-CAPTIONED bubble swallowed the rest of the page.** WT: `[Alert or speech bubble] … Giftedness isn't just something you have…superpower.` then `[image] <superman iStock>`, then `[body] This module will help you:` + bullets + `[body] You can work at your own pace…` + `[video]` + a 2nd `[speech bubble]`. The bundle swallowed everything from `This module will help you` to the 2nd bubble (the human renders all of it as normal page content). Neither existing section-break terminator fired: `body_terminates_after_face` needs a captured `[front]`/`[back]` member (none — the bubble text rides on the invocation itself), and `body_terminates_after_table` needs a captured table (none — it's inline-authored). **Robust fix (`InteractiveScanner.#swallowMembers` + data):** new `member_rule.body_terminates_after_invocation_text_types: ["speechBubble"]` — for a SELF-CAPTIONED widget (content rides on its own invocation's trailing text), a `[Body]` ELEMENT after the invocation (which already carries the bubble text) is the writer RESUMING FREE BODY → terminate. This is the inline-authored sibling of rounds 25/31/32 (`body_terminates_after_face`/`_after_table`): same section-break family, for a widget whose "face" is its invocation text.
