## 2026-06-16 (round 28) — paired-data: table-based IMAGE|caption carousel auto-build + shared column-role detector (build 260616.8)

Chris's ask: when a simple-interactive tag is followed by content structured as **two lots of data paired** for that interactive (a 2-column table), interpret it — for ALL simple auto-built interactives — via a **flexible, content-based column-ROLE rule**, not exact-tag rules. **Measured first** (`reference/Paired_Data_Table_Findings.md`, tools `_measure_paired.cjs` / `_probe_bundle.cjs`): the only paired-data TABLE form not yet consumed is the **carousel `image | caption` table** (the round-27 `#carousel` built member-VIDEO carousels only). flipCard/speechBubble/hintSlider already consume their `front|back` / `image|text` table; accordion/tabs are member-based by design. So this round closes the carousel table gap and factors out the shared detector.

1. **Table IMAGE|caption carousel — built, conservative (the OSGM501-01 trigger).** `InteractiveBuilder.#carousel` now dispatches by CONTENT: a carousel with exactly one captured table and NO video member → `#carouselImageTable` (the video path is preserved verbatim as `#carouselVideo`). Each data row → `div.item.image > img + div.carousel-caption>p`; the iStock id (digits after `gm` in the cell's URL) → `images/iStock-<id>.jpg`, image honours Mode P/D; alt is non-derivable → `alt=""`. A leading single-cell `[Title]` row and an `Images | Text` column-label row are dropped (content-based `#isCarouselTitleOrLabelRow`); a trailing `[body]` paragraph after the table is the writer **resuming free body** (the human renders it as a `<p>` after the carousel — OSGM501-01 "Video games offer…") and is appended via `carousel.trailing_body`, not lost. Data: `Emit_Templates.interactive_builders.carousel` (`item_image`, `image_mode_P/D`, `filename_istock`, `trailing_body`).

2. **Shared column-ROLE detector (the general principle).** New `InteractiveBuilder` helpers `#cellMediaUrl` (image cell = any non-video http URL, marker/separator-independent), `#imageCaptionPair` (a 2-cell row → image+caption in EITHER order, iStock-derivable, ≤1 red span/cell, clean residual, single-paragraph caption), `#isCarouselTitleOrLabelRow`. These generalise the speechBubble `#isImageCell` test onto a content-based rule robust to writer deviation (`[carousel N]` vs `[slide N]` vs none, `" / "` vs newline, title row present/absent). Per Chris's fallback clause, the carousel's table path was **added WITHOUT disturbing** flipCard/speechBubble/hintSlider (they stay build-neutral — A/B byte-identical, see below); the detector is shared and available to unify them later under their own A/B.

3. **New reusable verifier `_verify_image_carousel.cjs`** — compares each built slide's **image-id + caption** to the human gold (word-overlap, like the other verifiers), and classes an id-miss whose caption still matches a human slide as a faithful **developer image-swap** (the writer's pasted URL ≠ the final asset, e.g. OSGM301 slide 1 `gm1204995759`→human `iStock-1204996128`) rather than a defect.

The empty-image text form (AGH soil carousels) and irregular multi-column layouts (OSAH401) and developer-diverged `[carousel]`s (AGH1002 renders no carousel) all fall back.

**Result + gates (all held):** **OSGM301 + OSGM501** build image carousels (10 slides), `_verify_image_carousel.cjs` **0 defects** (1 faithful dev-image-swap); the other **206** carousel modules all fall back. Regenerated OSGM301/OSGM501. **compare_structure 86.9% exact / 1.9% over-nesting (101 EXTRA)** — neutral (exact 4593→4594; built carousels are excluded as wrapper-catalogue `carousel`); tags **100% (9557/9557)**; sentinels OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7; **video-carousel verifier 10 built / 0 mismatched** (the refactor is video-neutral); **flipCard + speechBubble verifiers BYTE-IDENTICAL via A/B** (flipCard CEDO102 1 / MXDB302 4 / TRR114 4 / XMES201 5; speechBubble 0 defects) — the carousel change does not touch their code. **body_compare over-capture 46→47** is the documented denominator artifact (rounds 20/22): building OSGM501-01's carousel correctly moves its 5 captions into the excluded carousel, shrinking Claude's free-body so a **pre-existing un-built dragAndDrop** (Activity 1A, biggest_banner=dragAndDrop 2859 chars — NOT the carousel) crosses the 40% line; empty unchanged at 56, runaway 7. ## 2026-06-15 (round 27) — carousel auto-build (video carousels only) + slideshow trailing-media exemption (build 260616.7)

Chris asked to build carousels if "fairly consistent and straightforward". **Researched first** (`reference/Carousel_Build_Assessment.md`): carousels are MORE varied than the prior clean widgets — TWO authoring forms (member `[Slide N]` + table-based), 3 slide content types (video/image/text), capture blockers (`heading_is_terminator` cuts text slides; `trailing_media_extract` trims trailing video slides), non-derivable image paths, and 416 distinct human shapes. So only the **homogeneous video carousel** is cleanly, content-derivably buildable. Chris chose "boundary fix + build video carousels".

1. **Scanner trailing-media exemption (prerequisite).** A trailing `[video]`/`[audio]` in a SLIDESHOW widget (carousel, rotateBanner) is the LAST SLIDE, not post-widget media — `trailing_media_extract` was trimming it (the slide rendered standalone after the widget, and an auto-build would then DUPLICATE it). New `member_rule.trailing_media_extract_exempt_types: ["carousel","rotateBanner"]`; `InteractiveScanner.#trimTrailingMedia` skips them.

2. **`InteractiveBuilder.#carousel` — VIDEO carousels only, conservative.** Walks `bundle.memberItems`; if every member is a YouTube video (or a structural `[Slide N]` marker / blank line) with no caption/heading text, builds `div.row.carousel > div.col-md-12.col-12.viewer > [div.item.video > {video.youtube embed}]+` (one slide per video). **Returns null (keeps the placeholder)** the moment a slide is a non-YouTube URL, carries caption/heading TEXT, is an image, has < 2 videos (1 video is just a video), or the bundle merged extra widget types. Data: `interactive_builders.carousel`. Image/text/mixed carousels (ENGJ301's video+text) stay honest placeholders. The exact human classes vary by series (`item` vs `item.video`, `videoSection icon` vs plain, `col-12` vs `col-md-12`), so this matches on CONTENT (video IDs), not byte-for-byte — a working carousel beats a placeholder.

3. **Reusable verifier `_verify_carousel.cjs`** (video-ID comparison vs the human gold, like the other widget verifiers). **Result: 10 carousels built across EXPFUN02/03 + ENGJ301, 27 video slides, 0 mismatched IDs** — every built slide's video is in the human carousel; EXPFUN05/TEFUN08 (image-mislabelled / text) correctly fell back.

## 2026-06-15 (round 26) — WT-triangulated containment: callout WRAPS a following table (empty-alert fix) (build 260616.6)

Driven by Chris's OSGM501-01 `[Alert]`. **Triangulation:** WT = `[Alert]` (no text) → a 2-column table (`[image]` | `[speechbubble]` support text) → `[End page]`. **Human:** the alert CONTAINS the table (image col-md-4 + text col-md-8 grid). **Claude (broken):** the alert rendered EMPTY ("RED FLAG: Empty [alert]…") and the table was lifted OUT into a separate speechBubble placeholder — two failures: the strict-callout gather only collects black TEXT (a table-as-content → empty box), and the scanner pulls the interactive-in-table out of the callout.

**The breakdown:** the strict containment model (round 3, the OSAI201 anti-over-nesting fix) holds only the following black-text run; when a writer's callout content is a TABLE, the box is empty. **The robust rule (measured: 18 modules have a callout-immediately-followed-by-table; the human renders the table inside):** a CONTENT callout (one with `wrap_content` — alert/important) that has NO black text of its own and is immediately followed by a TABLE spans to CONTAIN it (and any widget the scanner built from it), in a new **"span-wrap"** mode. **Critically it is TIGHTLY bounded** — `#closeSpanWrap` closes the callout the instant its one table/widget has rendered, so it holds EXACTLY that content and can never wrap the free body that follows. (A first attempt closing only at the next heading/section/page over-captured: compare_structure over-nesting jumped 100→126 / 2.4%; the immediate close brought it back to **101 / 1.9%**.) `ContentConverter.#calloutWrapsStructured` + `#closeSpanWrap`; data `callouts.containment.wrap_close_heading_max` (3) kept as a belt-and-braces autoClose fallback. Whakataukī/text callouts unaffected (no `wrap_content` / they have their own text).

**Verified + gates:** OSGM501-01 alert is no longer empty — the support content renders INSIDE it, tightly bounded (689 chars); empty-callout flags corpus-wide **119 → 97** (22 fixed); compare_structure **86.9% exact / 1.9% over-nesting** (both within gate), tags 100%, body over-capture 46 (−1), sentinels held (OSAI201 4 / MXEX401 7 / OSAH401 5 / ANZH205 7), flipCard 12 / speechBubble 0. The small exact dip (87.1→86.9) is the human GRID-unpacking the table inside the alert (col-md-4 + col-md-8) vs Claude wrapping the widget/table — the deferred layout-table-to-grid item (P1/P2/P6), not a new bug; structurally the content is now correctly INSIDE the alert.

## 2026-06-15 (round 25) — WT-triangulated containment: whakataukī proverb-only + face-widget [Body] resumption (build 260616.5)

Driven by Chris pointing at XGF9001-00: the whakataukī was absorbing the explanation paragraph, and the flipCard placeholder was absorbing the non-interactive body that follows it. The mandate: triangulate the WT → human, find where the interpretation breaks, and make the rule ROBUST to variations (not a one-off patch). Both done WT-first; note both slipped past `body_compare` (XGF9001-00 = 0 over-capture — the page is widget-heavy on both sides, so the ≥40%-of-body threshold isn't met), which is why the aggregate gate never flagged them — the new `--diff` mode does.

1. **Whakataukī absorbed the commentary — FIXED, robustly.** WT: `[Whakataukī] <reo> – <english>` then a blank line then a long commentary paragraph (NO marker) then `[Body]`. The strict-callout gather grabbed the whole black run up to `[Body]`, so the commentary landed inside `.whakatauki`; and the reo/english didn't split because the separator was "–" not "|". **The robust rule (measured 137/147 human `.whakatauki` hold exactly the 2 proverb `<p>`, only 4 hold a long paragraph):** a proverb callout holds ONLY its leading SHORT line(s) — `ContentConverter.#gatherProverb` stops at the first paragraph longer than `proverb_max_chars` (200) or after `proverb_max_paragraphs` (2) and leaves the rest UN-consumed → free body; reo/english split on `|`, `–`, OR `—` (spaced, so hyphenated words/ranges are safe). Handles the variations: one-line reo–english, reo+english on two lines, commentary of any length. Data: `callouts.by_tag.whakatauki.proverb_only`. Verified XGF9001-00: `.whakatauki` now = 2 proverb `<p>` (split on the en-dash); the commentary is free body, not lost.

2. **Face-widget absorbed the following body — FIXED, content-shape rule.** WT: 2 flipcards (`[Front]`/`[Back]`) then `[Body] This module is here…`. The scanner swallowed the `[Body]` as a member. The round-19/20 notes deferred this because `[Body]` is ambiguous (SSFUN07's flip BACKS are `[Body]`). **The robust discriminator (from the boundary bank signatures):** a FACE widget — `signature_subtags` has front/back and NEVER `body` (flipCard, speechBubble) — that has ALREADY captured a face treats a following `[Body]` ELEMENT as the writer resuming free body → terminate. A `[Body]`-based flip form with no faces (SSFUN07) never trips it. Data: `member_rule.body_terminates_after_face`; `InteractiveScanner.#swallowMembers`. Verified XGF9001-00: "This module is here…" is now FREE BODY (outside any widget); flipCard verifier unchanged at 12 defects with SSFUN07 unaffected, speechBubble 0 defects.

**Standing procedure (Chris's mandate, now the rule for every inconsistency):** for any perceived Claude-vs-human difference, (a) pull the WT region with the human + Claude via `wt_triangulate.py` / `full_compare.py --diff`, (b) find where the writer's tagging was mis-interpreted, (c) derive the rule from a corpus-wide MEASUREMENT so it generalises to similar variations, (d) implement data-first, (e) regenerate + re-gate. Not "handle this exact format" — handle the class.

## 2026-06-15 (round 24) — per-page DIFF mode (un-blinded on widget pages) + acks dedup + placeholder title (build 260616.4)

Chris uploaded XGF9001-00 (Claude) vs XGF9001-00.0 (human) — obviously very different — and asked why the comparison kept missing it. **Two root causes, both fixed:**

- **The comparator was BLIND on widget-heavy pages.** `full_compare.py` skips widget subtrees on BOTH sides; XGF9001's human page builds everything inside widgets (rotateBanner, flipCards, accordion, speechBubble, choice tiles) and Claude placeholders them, so the tool compared only **3 text-matched elements**. New `full_compare.py --diff <claudeFile> <humanFile>` does a true per-ELEMENT `difflib` diff with NO widget-skipping — it lists every concrete difference (it immediately surfaced the title, the dropped Te Reo h1, the two-column `paddingR`/`paddingL`+`div.item` menu, `h4` vs `h5`, "Understand" vs "Understand:", and a bold-boundary bug `Identity awareness.)` inside the `<b>`).
- **Filename naming varies a LOT.** XGF9001's human files are `-N.N.html` (hyphen) not the dominant `_N.N.html`; corpus-wide there are 8+ shapes (`_N.N` 1276, `-N.N` 238, `.N` 171, `-N` 167, `.html` 51, …). `page_key` pairs the overview correctly, but XGF9001's human has 15 pages (editorial sub-pages `-01.1/-01.2`) vs Claude's 7 — the MXDI102 non-derivable sub-pagination class.

**Two derivable bugs the diff exposed — FIXED:**
1. **Acks duplication.** The writer pasted iStock 1957478548 (the compass) ~10× across XGF9001; each media-list row became an entry and `AcksBuilder` listed all of them → the asset acknowledged **13×** on page 0. The human acknowledges an asset ONCE per lesson. **Fix:** `AcksBuilder` now de-duplicates exact ack lines WITHIN each lesson group (per-group, since an asset legitimately recurs across lessons). XGF9001-00: 13 → 5 (once per lesson group it appears in).
2. **Placeholder title shipped as `<h1>`.** WT `[TITLE BAR] My Inner Compass | Te Reo` — "Te Reo" ("the language") is the writer's PLACEHOLDER for the translation, which the human replaced with "Te Takinga o taku wairua" (not in the WT). Claude shipped the literal "Te Reo" as a title. **Fix:** `header.title_split.placeholder_titles` (["te reo"]) — a title-half matching it is dropped and red-flagged, not emitted as an `<h1>`. XGF9001-00 now shows just "My Inner Compass".

**Honest classification of the remaining XGF9001-00 differences:** most are **Phase-1 by design** (the human BUILDS rotateBanner/flipCard/accordion/speechBubble/choice-tiles; Claude ships honest placeholders) — expected, not bugs. The rest are the already-catalogued patterns from round 23: column-width monoculture (P1), heading-level drift `h4`/`h5` (P4), menu two-column layout (P2), and a missing section heading (P5). The `--diff` mode makes all of them visible per page now.

## 2026-06-15 (round 23) — FULL element-by-element diff + the `<b>`/`<i>` markup convention (build 260616.3)

Chris asked for an EXHAUSTIVE element-by-element comparison of every Claude page against its human counterpart — find ALL discrepancies and group the conversion errors into patterns. New tool `reference/tests/full_compare.py` (+ `full_compare.json`): for 908 paired pages it compares the full tag+class inventory across `#header`/`#body`/`#footer`/`.acks` AND, for every text-MATCHED content element, the exact discrepancy (heading level / element tag / col-width / wrapper chain / duplication) — surfacing recurring conversion errors that `compare_structure.py` (matched-chain summary only) can't. Full grouped write-up + derivable/non-derivable labels: `reference/Full_Element_Comparison_Findings.md` (patterns P1–P9).

**Fixed from the analysis — inline markup convention.** The Te Kura house style is PRESENTATIONAL, not semantic: measured across all human pages `<b>` **11,259** vs `<strong>` 277, and `<i>` **4,822** vs `<em>` 144 — yet Claude emitted `<strong>` 10,632 / `<em>` 6,100 and ZERO `<b>`/`<i>`. **Fix (data-first):** `Emit_Templates.elements.inline_format` → `<b>{content}</b>` / `<i>{content}</i>` (was the unused `<strong>`/`<em>`), and `ContentConverter.#inlineMarkup` now READS that config (it previously hard-coded the tags) so `**bold**`→`<b>`, `*italic*`→`<i>`; the callout bold-lead fallback `<p><strong>`→`<p><b>` for consistency. Verified ENGS301 (`<strong>` 41→0, `<i>` 55). Invisible to the structure gates (inline markup sits inside a matched element's text, not a separate content node). **Deferred (not derivable from `**`/`*` markdown):** the human's `<u>` (205) and `<br>` (10,136) have no source marker, and most `<br>` are inside human-built widgets — recorded as a limitation.

**Patterns surfaced but NOT auto-fixed (documented, ranked by leverage):** P1 column-width monoculture + P2 row over-emission + P6 layout-tables-kept-raw all share one root — a writer LAYOUT table the human unpacks into a `col-md-N` grid (the single biggest structural gap, ~130–190 modules; needs a layout-vs-data table detector). P4 heading-level drift (`h3→h4` 432: writer digits unreliable, human re-levels by hierarchy — non-derivable, but worth measuring `body_shift:0`). P5 heading/list under-detection (`h5→p` 399, `li→p` 111 — measure WT-backed vs editorial). P8 `.interactive` still under-emitted (Δ−279 — extendable per-type). Expected non-errors confirmed: stickyNav dropped by policy, cv2 placeholders vs built widgets.

## 2026-06-15 (round 22) — strict Claude-vs-human diff: duplicated lesson heading + bilingual overview title count (build 260616.2)

Driven by Chris's observation that lesson headings were duplicated in the Claude output. A new strict per-page comparison tool (`reference/tests/strict_compare.py`) confirmed it as a CORPUS-WIDE basic disconnect that `compare_structure.py` misses (it only scores text-MATCHED elements, so a duplicate heading with no human counterpart isn't flagged). Two derivable, gate-clean fixes from the strict diff:

1. **Duplicated lesson title — FIXED (the big one Chris flagged).** `PageSplitter` harvests the lesson title from the page's first heading (`[H2] Lesson 1 Judge a book by its cover`) into the header `<h1>`, but the same heading item stayed in the body and `ContentConverter` rendered it AGAIN as an `<h3>`. **Measured: 683 of 887 Claude lesson pages (77%) duplicated the title** vs only 35/758 (5%) in the human gold. **Fix:** `ContentConverter` now consumes the FIRST body heading whose folded text equals the page's promoted lesson title (`#pageLessonTitle`) — the human shows the lesson title once, in the header. Only the first body heading is a candidate (a deeper legitimate repeat is untouched). Verified ENGS301-01 ("Judge a book by its cover" 2→1), AGH1002, etc. **Corpus result: strict-diff `dup_title` 525 → 23 (3%) — now BELOW the human's own 57.** Gate effect: compare_structure exact chains hold at **87.2%**; total Claude content elements drop ~640 (the removed duplicates); over-nesting **absolute count unchanged at 103** (the % reads 2.0% only because the matched denominator shrank — no new over-nesting). body_compare over-capture 41 → **47**: a denominator ARTIFACT, not real — removing a free-body heading shrinks Claude's body so 6 borderline pages' widgets cross body_compare's 40%-of-body threshold (e.g. AGH1009-09 at exactly 40%; the human "free blocks" are unchanged, the widget captures nothing new). Same threshold sensitivity the round-20 note describes.

2. **Bilingual overview title count — overview now emits BOTH split languages (net-positive, but surfaced a separate bug).** The header emitted `min(registry h1_count, available)` titles, popping from the END — so a bilingual `[TITLE BAR]` capped at `h1_count.overview=1` dropped the SECOND title. Critically the pop kept `english` and dropped `teReo`, and where the round-7 Course-backup had put the **subject/course name** in `english`, the cap kept the JUNK and hid the REAL title (ENGC101 showed only "English", hiding "Ways we communicate"). **Fix (`SkeletonBuilder`):** the overview emits every language the WT split produced (the split is the derivable truth). This fixed 5 genuine bilingual under-counts AND un-hid the real titles. The strict `h1_count` metric stayed ~flat (175→171) because it ALSO exposed a **separate, pre-existing title-PARSING bug** (now flagged, not yet fixed): the subject/course name leaks into a title h1 on a handful of modules (ENGC101 "English", MXDI103 "Discovering Mathematics", BLL252/254 "Blended Literacy Learning"), and XMES201's title-bar parsing emits literal garbage ("…MODULE TITLE TE REO:…"). These need a dedicated title-pipeline pass (subject/course-name exclusion + label stripping + revisiting the Course-backup), independent of the title COUNT. The remaining overview under-counts (26) are NON-derivable (the WT title has no separable second language).

Other strict-diff signals triaged as NON-derivable / deferred: **heading-level drift** (rose to 47% AFTER the de-dup UN-MASKED it — the duplicate `<h3>` had been coincidentally matching the human's first heading level; the writer's `[H5]` etc. are unreliable logical levels and the human re-levels by document hierarchy, e.g. ENGS301's WT `[H5]` → human `<h3>` → not a fixed shift, so not safely derivable without semantic structure); **menu present-on-one-side** (22% — largely the round-10 source-limitation class: lesson menus authored outside the WT); the **title-parsing junk** above. All recorded in `strict_compare.py` output for ongoing tracking.

## 2026-06-15 (round 20) — over-capture: explicit close markers terminate the widget (build 260615.9)

Continued the over-capture class. The next clean, safe sub-cause: a widget that swallows **past its own close marker**. Two parts, both grounded in WT semantics (a close marker ends a container):

- **Part A (scanner):** `#swallowMembers` now terminates on **any `CONTAINER_CLOSE` directive**. Before, only the handful of `end X` canonicals that happened to be in `terminators_absolute` stopped a widget; `[End Carousel]`, `[End of clickdrop 1]`, `[End slideshow]`, `[end task]` (all CONTAINER_CLOSE) were swallowed. One line.
- **Part B (lexicon):** the **suffix** close forms now resolve to CONTAINER_CLOSE. `[Carousel ends here]` (×17 in the corpus), `[accordion ends]`/`[accordion ends here]` (×23), `[modal ends]`, `[Tabs end here]`, `[coloured box ends here]` were matching the *embedded widget name* first (→ INTERACTIVE) so they OPENED a new empty widget AND failed to close the open one (ENGJ301 had 8 `[Carousel ends here]`). Added as aliases of `end other`; verified `[Insert carousel]` still opens normally.

**Result (full regen):** over-capture **45 → 41**, runaway-absorption **9 → 7**. Pages genuinely freed: ENGJ301-01 (8 `[Carousel ends here]`), CEDO501-12 (`[End of clickdrop 1]`), ENGR102-05 — all off the over-capture list, content now correctly free body, **0 literal `ends here]` leaks**. **No regression on the hard gates:** structure **87.2% exact / 1.9% over-nesting** (exact COUNT rose 4551→4625; the 0.2pp dip is denominator — more free body is now correctly exposed to match), tags **100% (9557/9557)**, flip-card **12 pre-existing defects** (unchanged), speech-bubble 0 defects, sentinels held.

**Honest read of the metric:** the **empty** count ticked **60 → 66** and so the *broken-page count is roughly flat*. These are NOT new breakage — they are widgets now **correctly bounded** to their (sometimes <40-char) real content, which body_compare's empty threshold flags; 56 of the 66 empty pages have **negative `lost_blocks`** (Claude renders MORE free body than the human — nothing buried). So round 20 is a **correctness/placement** improvement (over-capture and runaway both down, content freed) rather than a broken-page-count reduction.

**Remaining over-capture (41) — the genuinely hard cases:** `[Body]`-after-widget that is type-dependent (a section break for HIS1007's sources accordion, the widget's own backs for SSFUN07's flip-cards); developer divergence (HIS1007-02 — the writer said "arrange the sources in an accordion" but the human rendered them as free body, so Claude's faithful accordion looks like over-capture); and widgets with no close marker at all (XDLS912, MXDI202, CEDK501). These need a per-widget/content-shape heuristic, not another terminator.

## 2026-06-15 (round 19) — body-breakdown fix #3: inline infoTrigger over-capture + flip-cell guard (build 260615.8)

Started the **over-capture** class (59 pages — a widget eats body the human keeps free). Diagnosed on the worst pages (HIS1007-02, SSFUN07-00, CEDK501-03): the cause is **heterogeneous** across 12 widget types, with two distinct mechanisms. The single biggest CLEAN sub-cause is **inline infoTrigger** — `[rollover/hover/mouseover definition: …]` markers embedded mid-paragraph. The human renders these as an inline `<span class="infoTrigger" info="…">word</span>` tooltip (measured 1,669 inline spans vs 232 block divs), but the scanner opened a block widget that swallowed the rest of the page (SSFUN07-00 ate 77 free blocks; PHE1008-00 at 93%).

**Fix (data-first, extends the round-18 inline-marker mechanism):**
- New bank field `member_rule.standalone_inline_markers: ["infoTrigger"]`. A STANDALONE inline infoTrigger (in body text) is dropped and its surrounding text renders as free body — so it can't eat the page. The hover-definition payload is deferred with the interactive build (Phase 1 renders the annotated word as readable plain text).
- Deliberately NOT added to `inline_markers` (the in-widget *absorb* list): inside an open widget an infoTrigger TERMINATES as before. Absorbing it corrupted ENGS101's compound-word flip-cards (the `[Rollover definition]` CS-notes in the card region got pulled into the build). The two roles are now separate lists.
- **Flip-cell guard** (`InteractiveBuilder.#flipCell`): stopping the over-capture *unblocked* an ENGS101 flip-card the over-capturing infoTrigger had previously eaten — exposing a pre-existing builder bug (when an istock `[LINK:…]` is link-extracted from a flip cell, the leftover image-label + word, e.g. `Snowman / Snowman`, rendered as a duplicated `Snowman<br>Snowman`). The guard falls back to the honest placeholder when a flip cell resolves to identical duplicated halves — ENGS101 now safely falls back instead of mis-building.

**Result (full regen of the 77 infoTrigger modules):** over-capture **59 → 45** (−14), empty **69 → 60** (side benefit), any-breakdown pages **135 → 112**. SSFUN07-00 / PHE1008-00 over-capture gone. **No regression:** structure **87.4% exact / 2.0% over-nesting**, tags **100% (9557/9557)**; flip-card verifier back to its **12 pre-existing defects** (A/B-proven: the inline-marker mechanism is build-neutral; ENGS101's +5 was the unblocked-then-guarded build, now a clean fallback); speech-bubble 26 exact / 3 copy-edit / 0 defects; sentinels held.

**Remaining over-capture (45) — the harder, type-dependent causes (next):** `[Body]` AFTER a widget's data is a section break in some modules (HIS1007's sources accordion) but the widget's OWN content in others (SSFUN07's flip-card backs are `[Body]` paragraphs — measured `class="back"` in the gold), so a blanket `[Body]` terminator is unsafe; plus carousel/clickDrop/accordion boundaries with no explicit terminator. These need a per-widget or content-shape heuristic, not a single rule.

## 2026-06-15 (round 18) — body-breakdown fix #2: empty-bundle guard + inline-marker handling (build 260615.7)

The big remaining body-breakdown class was **EMPTY interactive containers** (204 pages). A diagnostic over the 12 worst modules classified the empty bundles: a handful were END markers (`[X ends]`, 15) / insert markers (2), but the **dominant cause (59)** was *recognised-but-content-less* widget markers — above all `[highlight text]` / `[word select]`. These are **not standalone widgets**: the human renders them as an inline highlight ON the surrounding container (e.g. a flip-card's back face carries the `wordHighlighter` class). Treating them as block widgets did two kinds of damage on XGF9001: inside a flip-card the `[highlight text]` *terminated* it ("Being [highlight text] gifted means…" split into a 12-char back + a stray wordSelect holding the rest), and standalone it opened a wordSelect that *swallowed* the following paragraph (#7 ate 1,537 chars the human keeps free).

**Fix — two parts, data-first:**
1. **Empty-bundle guard** (`ContentConverter.#interactivePlaceholder`): a bundle that captured no content (no member text, table, media or heading) no longer renders a full orange placeholder box — it emits a **compact red flag** (the marker is still surfaced + listed in the manifest, but the page is not littered with empty shells). This neutralises the END/insert/instruction empties at the output.
2. **Inline-marker handling** (`InteractiveScanner` + new bank field `member_rule.inline_markers: ["wordSelect","wordHighlighter"]`): inside an open widget an inline marker is **absorbed as a plain member** (never a terminator) so the host's text stays whole; standalone, it is **not** a widget at all — the marker literal is dropped and its own-line text re-exposed as normal **free body**. Both behaviours are driven by the bank list, so the set is tunable without code.

**Result (full 192-module regen):** EMPTY containers **204 → 69** (−66%); any-breakdown pages **264 → 135** (−49%); XGF9001-00/-02/-06 now fully clean (its flip-card backs are whole and the highlighted paragraphs render as free body — 0 literal `[highlight text]` leakage). **No regression:** structure **87.4% exact / 2.0% over-nesting** (unchanged), tags **Python 100% (9557/9557, 0 real failures) / JS 100%**, sentinels held (OSAI201 4, MXEX401 7, OSAH401 5, ANZH205 7). **Build-neutral, proven by A/B:** re-running `_verify_flipcard.cjs` with `inline_markers` emptied vs set gives **byte-identical** results (12 pre-existing defects either way — glossary-header/table issues from earlier rounds, NOT this change); `_verify_speechbubble.cjs` 26 exact / 3 copy-edit / **0 defects**.

**Remaining (next, in order):** the residual **over-capture (59)** is the root-cause-A terminator class — a widget swallowing many paragraphs with no `[Body]`/heading-after-data terminator (e.g. SSFUN07-00, XDLS912-02); the **runaway-absorption (10)** is a real `[Activity N]` legitimately + over-eagerly absorbing ≥4 types (XGF9001-04). The pre-existing flip-card glossary-header defects (ARFUN04 "Terms"/"Definitions", MXDB302, XMES201) are a builder issue, separate from body placement.

## 2026-06-15 (round 17) — body-breakdown fix #1: scanner terminator hardening (widget sub-numbers ≠ activity ids) (build 260615.6)

New diagnostic first: `reference/Body_Content_Breakdown_Audit.md` + `reference/tests/body_compare.py` (re-runnable) — a per-page #body content-PLACEMENT comparison (Claude vs human) that finds whole pages the converter breaks: a widget OVER-CAPTURES the page, an EMPTY container, content BURIED in a widget. It excludes widget subtrees on both sides, so it measures free body LOST to a widget (no false positives on legitimately single-widget pages). Baseline: **70 over-capture, 23 runaway-absorption (one bundle ≥4 widget types), 257 empty, 324 broken pages** of 1,188.

**Root cause (diagnosed on XGF9001-00):** `InteractiveScanner` captured the number on an interactive tag as an `activityId` — meant for `[Activity 7 drag and drop]`, but it also fired for a widget's own PANEL index (`[Flipcard 1]`, `[Accordion 2]`). A fake `activityId` then turned on `same_activity_multi_widget`, so the flipCard absorbed the following 2nd flipcard, BOTH accordions, a speechBubble and the `[Body]`/"cultures" text — 31 members, the whole rest of the page.

**Fix (2 surgical scanner edits, no data shape change):**
1. The number on an interactive span becomes an `activityId` ONLY when the span genuinely carries the `[Activity]` tag (a panel index never does).
2. In `#swallowMembers`, a new interactive of the **same** widget type is always absorbed (multi-panel: accordion strips, flip-card decks stay one bundle), but a **different** type is absorbed only inside a REAL `[Activity N]` (BLL155 carousel+selfCheck preserved) — otherwise it TERMINATES. A flipCard can no longer swallow the next accordion.

**Result:** XGF9001-00's runaway flipCard 31 members → **4** (just its 2 cards); its over-capture flag is gone. Corpus: broken pages **324 → 264** (60 fixed); **runaway-absorption 23 → 10** (more than halved); over-capture 70 → 59; empty 257 → 204 (side benefit). **No regression:** structure 87.4% exact / 2.0% over-nesting, tags Python 99.99% / JS 100%; sentinels held (OSAI201 4, MXEX401 7, OSAH401 5, ANZH205 7); BLL155 carousel+selfCheck and all accordion/tabs panels still bundle correctly.

**Remaining (next, in order):** the EMPTY widgets (204) are mostly `[X ends here]`/`[Insert X]`/instruction markers parsed as OPENERS (body-breakdown fix #2); the residual over-capture (59) is a widget swallowing many paragraphs with no terminator (`[Body]`/heading-after-data).

## 2026-06-15 (round 16) — scaffolding audit #4: alert/important content wrapped in row>col-12 (build 260615.5)

Audit issue #4 (flattened callouts). Measured the human's alert internals: content sits in `alert > div.row > div.col-12` ~**78%** of the time (vs the converter's direct `<p>`), and the inner column is **col-12 in 94%** of cases. **Fix (data + one line):** new `Emit_Templates.callouts.content_wrap` (`row>col-12`) + a per-tag `wrap_content:true` on `alert`/`important`; `ContentConverter.#calloutOpen` wraps the STRICT content run when the flag is set. whakataukī/quote keep their direct `<p>`s (no flag), matching the gold. Worried this would breach the over-nesting gate (the ~22% the human leaves direct), I MEASURED it on a 25-module callout sample first: exact 87.4%→88.2%, over-nesting 3.2%→3.1% — net positive, so shipped.

**Result (192 modules):** `callout:alert > row` **0 → 779** (human 719) — alerts now structured like the human; direct `alert > p` 1152 → 138. **compare_structure exact chains 86.6% → 87.4%** (best to date), **over-nesting held at 2.0%** (no breach), tags Python 99.99% / JS 100%. Regenerated the 148 alert-bearing modules only.

**Interconnection (big win for #1):** plain `col-12` — issue #1's single largest gap — went **76 → 857** (human 1317), because the wrapped alert content now lives in `col-12`. So #4 closed most of the #1 `col-12` gap that had no standalone fix.

**Honest notes:** (a) Claude now wraps ~100% of alert/important vs the human's ~78%, a slight over-wrap — but the over-nesting gate held, so it is within tolerance (the alertActivity/teacher variants the human leaves direct could be excluded later for an even tighter match). (b) The audit's raw `row` count rose 14,995 → 15,842 (1.43×→1.50×), but this is NOT a #3 regression: Claude was previously MISSING the alert-internal rows the human has (0 vs 719) and now matches them — compare_structure (the real structural measure) improved, confirming the added rows are correct.

## 2026-06-15 (round 15) — scaffolding audit #3: grouped rows (text flows into the row) (build 260615.4)

Audit issue #3 (over-rows / no grouping). Measured the human's row composition (excl. interactives): only **14% of human rows hold a single content child — 86% group 2+** (h+p, h+p+p, p+p+p dominant), whereas the converter's per-block policy gave nearly every block its own row (the ~1.6× over-count). **Fix (data + one code branch):** new `Emit_Templates.body_region.row_breaks.group_content` mode — **text and lists FLOW into the current row; a heading starts a fresh row (the text after it flows in); a hard block (media/table/callout/widget/activity/page) takes its own row.** `ContentConverter`'s `rowFor` gains the grouped branch (legacy per-block kept behind `group_content:false`).

**Result (192 modules):** `row` 17,244 → **14,995** (ratio 1.64× → **1.43×**); compare_structure's per-page rows-ratio 2.54 → **2.19**; the human-vs-Claude single-child-row share moved from per-block's ~50% toward the human (Claude 36% vs human 29% on the sample). **Interconnection (as anticipated): issue #1 improved as a side effect** — `col-md-8` 17,206 → **14,956** (2.17× → **1.89×**), because fewer rows means fewer `col-md-8` wrappers (one per row). **No other issue moved** (p/img/headings/lists unchanged). **No regression:** structure exact chains 86.6% / over-nesting 2.0% (grouping is row+col-invariant to the wrapper-chain score), tags Python 99.99% / JS 100%, `<div>` balance intact. Regenerated all 192 modules (rows are everywhere).

**Honest residual:** #3 is reduced, not eliminated (Claude still 1.43×). The remainder is the human grouping MEDIA into a text row (h+p+img / h+p+iframe — the converter still breaks on media) and the human's grid/nested rows — both interconnected with image/grid handling (audit issue #5). Pushing further means flowing media into text rows, which needs the image-grid distinction to stay safe — deferred to #5.

A corpus-wide SCAFFOLDING audit (Claude vs human #body structure, all 192 modules) landed first — `reference/Scaffolding_Audit_Claude_vs_Human.md` + the re-runnable `reference/tests/scaffold_audit.py` (element inventory + parent→child hierarchy, no text-matching, so it covers all elements). Result: bare-table count **709 → 0**; verified AGH1008/MXDB202 now match the human structure. **Surgical:** no other audit signature moved (confirming #1 is not table-driven). No regression: structure 86.6% exact / 2.0% over-nesting, tags Python 99.99% / JS 100%. Regenerated the 172 table-bearing modules only (per the round-12 policy).
  - **Honest residual:** this fixes the table WRAPPER, not the table COUNT. The converter still over-produces tables where the human turned table content into NCEA quiz widgets (Phase 4, shown raw) and under-produces where a table sits inside a widget the converter doesn't build (e.g. BLL233's table-content tabs). ## 2026-06-15 (round 13) — flipCard + tabs auto-build (both at once) + two reusable verifiers (build 260615.2)

Chris asked for flipCard AND tabs implemented together in one pass. Both shipped, each built only for its clean subset (conservative, faithful-to-source) and scored row-by-row against the human. Gates after all edits, no regression: **tag Python 9556/9557 (99.99%) / JS 9557/9557 (100%); structure 86.6% exact / 2.0% over-nesting (190 modules, 0 errors); menu gate unchanged.** Regeneration was **selective per the round-12 policy** — only the 171 modules that contain a flipCard or tabs were rebuilt, not the whole corpus.

1. **flipCard auto-build (the grid).** Captured as one 2-column table — column 1 every card's FRONT, column 2 its BACK. `InteractiveBuilder.#flipCard` drops a leading column-label row, then renders each cell via `#flipCell`: an IMAGE when the cell carries an image reference (an iStock/.jpg URL, a `[LINK: …]`, an `[image]` tag, or the writer's "Link for photo/image" placeholder — the istock URL is link-extracted out of the cell) → an `<img>` honouring Mode P/D; otherwise the cell's BLACK text, with the writer's " / " (a spaced slash) → `<br>`. Output is `div.row.flipCardsContainer > div.col-… > div.flipCard > div.front + div.back`. Falls back (whole widget) when a text cell still carries a red instruction label (ENGI202's `[Front of flip card]` cards), a cell is empty/bulleted, or the capture is wider than two columns / more than one table.

2. **tabs auto-build (member-based, like accordion).** A `[tabs]` opener, then `[Tab N]` (heading = the tag's trailing text, e.g. "First person point of view") + body paragraph(s); a `[Tabs end here]` closer is ignored. `#tabs` builds `div.tabs > ul.nav-tabs (one li per heading) + div.tab-content (one tab-pane per tab)`. Plain heading + body TEXT only, ≥ 2 tabs — a DATA-TABLE pane (BLL233's letter tables), an image/nested pane, a missing heading, or red instruction text all fall back.

3. **Two reusable verifiers** (`_verify_flipcard.cjs`, `_verify_tabs.cjs`, clones of `_verify_speechbubble.cjs`) — capture each built widget, diff its text (card front/back; tab heading + pane) against the human gold with word-overlap so the developer's COPY-EDITS are not counted as defects. They also separate **developer DIVERGENCE** (the human file has no such widget — the `[flip card]`/`[tabs]` source was restructured/omitted, e.g. the CEDO301 holdout) from a real defect, since our build is still faithful to the WT. **Result: 0 real defects.** Every built widget matches the human exactly or modulo copy-edits; the only "misses" are confirmed against the WT source as human rewrites (e.g. CEDO102's back, where the human replaced "…like if we took all the biscuits…" with a different sentence — we keep the writer's, per Q1) or omissions.

**Coverage (honest).** 17 flipCard widgets + 1 tabs widget build across the corpus today — modest, because the rich majority correctly falls back: flipCards whose cells mix red instruction labels with content, and tabs whose panes are styled data tables (BLL233) or carry no heading. These are the next enhancement targets (render a tab's data-table pane; strip flipCard's `[Front of …]` labels rather than bailing) — both would lift coverage without loosening the never-guess rule. Answer-carrying / scored widgets remain Phase 4.

## 2026-06-15 (round 12) — no-table speechBubble investigation (NOT buildable) + the selective-regeneration policy (no engine change)

Two asks from Chris. **(1) The "no-table member form" was investigated and deliberately NOT built.** I had flagged it as the biggest remaining speechBubble coverage lever — that was wrong, from the raw "no-table" capture count before inspecting the shapes. Reading how the human designer actually translates these (31 modules sampled): the no-table bubbles are **not** a clean image+text pair (0 of 31 were). They are bespoke human compositions the converter must not fake — word-collection bubbles woven into colour-`<span>` sentences (ENGC101: the writer's loose words *cold / dark / nervous* become `The room was <span colour="secondary">cold</span> and <span…>dark</span>…`), `[speech bubble with hover]` + `[tile N]` + bullet widgets (OSGM201), video + `[Label]` markers (ANZH205), and "position speech bubble around image above" developer instructions where the image is a *separate* element (MXFL204). Every clean single image+text bubble is authored as the 1x2 TABLE we already build (round 11). Building the no-table form would mean guessing which image/words/layout the human intended — a direct violation of the project's iron rule — so it correctly stays a placeholder. The 28 table-form builds remain the complete safe set; no `app/`/`data/` change, no AppVersion bump, no regeneration.

**(2) Selective-regeneration policy — now standing for ALL future changes.** New `reference/Regeneration_Policy.md`: a change that touches an element present in only SOME modules regenerates ONLY the modules that contain it (in the WT or ANY HTML page — and then ALL of that module's pages); a change to an always-present concern (skeleton, header, menu, body wrappers, footer, acks, image mode, tag normalisation) regenerates every module. New tool `reference/tests/regen_affected.cjs` detects the affected set by searching `01-Finalized_Modules_/<CODE>/` (which holds both the human HTML and the parsed WT, so one search covers "WT or HTML") and prints the exact rebuild command. Verified: `speechBubble` → 93 of 192 modules; `--all` → 192. Baked into the discipline note below.

Driven by Chris's reprioritisation. Captures each built bubble and diffs its TEXT (+ iStock id) against the human gold, tolerant of the varied human bubble markup (`bubble-left/right/basic/top`, an inner `<div>` wrapper, HTML comments, `<p>` attributes). Word-set overlap separates a faithful build that differs only by the developer's COPY-EDITS (Q1 — not a defect) from a real error. **Result: 28 bubbles built across 12 modules, 0 real defects** — every build is exact or copy-edit-only vs the human (OSAI201/401/501, OSGM301/401/501, OSOH501, OSBY201, OSAH501, ENGR101, ENGS401, MXFU402).

**Known residual (honest):** the menu gate still flags ~20% of pages as "menu empty where the human has one" — but a large share are **source limitations**, not converter bugs: those lesson menus were **authored by the developer** and their text is **not in the Writers Template** (verified on MXFL204 lessons 2+). The converter correctly cannot reproduce content absent from the source (the ACK-TODO class). ## 2026-06-14 (round 9) — Phase 1 Part 2 begins: the auto-build framework + first real widget (hintSlider) (build 260614.1)

The converter now *builds* the easy interactives instead of only dumping placeholders. This round lays the framework and proves it end-to-end on the first widget, `hintSlider`, scored row-by-row against the human gold files. Governing rule held throughout: **never guess — the moment the captured data is ambiguous, fall back to the honest placeholder.**

1. **NEW `InteractiveBuilder.js` + `Emit_Templates.json → interactive_builders`** — the two-halves pattern the rest of the project uses: the *markup* of each widget lives as an editable, commented template in the data file (a developer can change wording/classes, or set `enabled:false`, with no code); the *code* only maps captured data into the slots. `ContentConverter.#interactivePlaceholder` asks the builder first; a returned string ships as the live widget (`bundle.built=true`), `null` falls through to the unchanged placeholder. Adding a widget = one data entry + one small `case`. Wired into `index.html` + `batch_convert.cjs` load order (before ContentConverter).

2. **hintSlider built** — from the human gold shape `div.hintSlider[hintCssFile="standard"] > div.hintRow > div.infoContainer > div.frontInfo>p + div.backInfo>p`. Conservative by construction: builds **only** from exactly **one** captured table that is exactly **two columns** (front | back). Anything else falls back — 3-column tables that fold in an image/audio (ENGI401, ENGR101, ENGS301), two-table captures (OSGM101), front/back written as free-text/paragraph rather than a table (Pattern 4 + the alternating-line Pattern 2 cases). No column is ever *guessed*.

3. **Header-row detection by the writer's own convention** — a table's first row is dropped as a column-label header when its cells are the writer's **red instruction text** (the structural signal, e.g. ENGR302's `Hint title | Information once slide`), OR match a data-tunable word list (`interactive_builders.hintSlider.header_label_keywords`: hint/slide/front/back/…). The red-text signal caught ENGR302's odd header that a word list never would — found via row-by-row diff (it had built 5 rows vs the human's 4) and fixed.

4. **Manifest reports build status** — `ManifestBuilder` header now counts *BUILT AUTOMATICALLY* vs *STILL UN-BUILT*, and every entry carries `Status: BUILT — live …` or `Status: un-built placeholder …` (the old "Phase 1 built NONE" note is gone).

**Coverage (21 hintSlider modules):** 9 of 30 captured hintSliders auto-build; the other 21 fall back safely. **Row-level verification vs human** (`reference/tests/_verify_hintslider.cjs`, reusable): all 9 match the human on row count, pairing and content — OSBY101 byte-identical; the only residual diffs are *human copy-edits the converter correctly does not invent* (added trailing full-stops, stripped bold off acronym initials like PPDAC's **A**nalysis, curly vs straight quotes, a source "oOne"→"one" typo). **Detection limits noted, not builder bugs:** where a module has several hintSliders, the clean one builds and the others (3-col/dark-variant/free-text) fall back. **No regression:** full structure compare holds **86.3% exact chains / 2.0% over-nesting** (188 compared, 0 errors); regression gate **99.99%** (9556/9557). Build badge → 260614.1.

## 2026-06-14 (round 8) — OSAI201/OSAI301 review: activity structure, interactive boundaries, an OOXML leak, numbering (build 260614)

Driven by Chris's side-by-side OSAI201 + OSAI301 human-vs-converter files. Five fixes, each verified against the gold file; full re-batch (190; TRR×2 refused) holds structure at **86.3% exact chains / 2.0% over-nesting**, gates green (Python 99.99%).

1. **Activity structure now matches the gold shape** — `div.activity > div.row > div.col-12 > <h3> title + instruction + widget`. Inner row/col added to `Emit_Templates.activity_wrapper`; ContentConverter promotes the activity's FIRST lead line to `<h3>` (the activity title). Measured against the human baseline (`reference/structural_catalogue/activity_interactive_audit`): inner `div.row` **0% → 100%**; `<h3>` titles **9% → 34%** (the interactive-owned path — standalone `[activity]` containers are a documented residual; human is 99%/93%). The `interactive` class was deliberately NOT forced (only 61% of human widget-activities carry it).

2. **Interactive boundary recognition for combined `[Activity][activity heading]` spans** — when an activity tag and its heading share one red span, the primary resolves to the heading (ELEMENT outranks CONTAINER_OPEN), which (a) let the previous widget swallow the new activity's lead and (b) lost the activity owner, splitting the widget. Fix (InteractiveScanner): detect an activity from ANY tag in the span (not just primary), and let the owner-lookback SKIP empty/noise spans instead of breaking on them. OSAI201 "Story prediction" dropQuiz: 3 fragments + bleed → **one** activity bundle.

3. **OOXML leak fixed (DocxExtractor)** — the run-text regex `/<w:t[^>]*>…<\/w:t>/` also matched `<w:tab/>` (`<w:t` + `ab/` + `>`), so a run mixing tabs with text emitted raw `<w:t xml:space="preserve">` / `<w:tab/>` onto the page (e.g. OSAI301 carousel slides + the "Story prediction" title). Tightened to `/<w:t(?: [^>]*)?>…/` so `<w:t` must be followed by a space or `>`. Removes raw XML corpus-wide.

4. **Activity numbering** — audit of all 376 parsed templates: number is inside the bracket `[Activity 1A]` 71%, just outside `[Activity] 1A` ~1%, absent ~28%; **~30% of modules reuse a number**. Rule adopted: capture the writer's number inside OR just outside the bracket, then de-duplicate per lesson in document order (a second `1A` → `1B`, mirroring the human renumbering); numberless activities left as-is. The deduped `activityId` flows into the wrapper `number` attr (ContentConverter `idOverride`). Verified OSAI301: "What AI can and can't do" **1A**, "Story prediction" **1B**.

5. **Reference tooling added (`reference/`)** — the full-page structural catalogue (`structural_catalogue/`: menu/body/footer fingerprints + tag→slot provenance, interactive-nesting stocktake, activity/interactive audit, `auto_check_rule.md` phase-1 mandate). `reference/tests/_deflate_raw_polyfill.cjs`: a CONDITIONAL Node-<20.4 shim for `DecompressionStream('deflate-raw')` (byte-identical zlib raw inflate; no-op on Node ≥20.4) so the batch harness runs on Node 18; preload with `node --require`.

## 2026-06-12 (round 4) — The BLL146 defects (spurious page, lost menu, unwrapped activities)

Driven by Chris's BLL146 conversion. Four distinct defects, each verified against the human gold files and fixed at the root:

1. **Spurious extra page / menu content in the body.** BLL-family templates write the intro as `[Title]`+`[Introduction]` (title-bar aliases), never `[MODULE INTRODUCTION]` — so the stray-[End page] repair (AR-1) never armed and the menu partition had no boundary. Fixes: AR-1 generalised (an overview `[end page]` is disregarded unless what follows opens a lesson — explicit boundary or "Lesson N" heading; `PageSplitter`), and the menu region now also ends at the first MID-document title-bar alias (`ContentConverter.#partitionItems`). Mid-doc `[Title]`/`[Introduction]` route through the heading rule in the SECTION_MARKER dispatch: a bare alias becomes its own word as an `<h3>` ("Introduction"), and a `[Title]` that merely repeats the module name is consumed (the header h1 already shows it) — both per the BLL146-0.0 gold file.
2. **Registry data error:** `BLL1.delta.menu_type.overview` said `none`; the corpus is unanimous (every BLL1xx overview has a simplified menu, 0 use tabs; 0/23 lessons have one). Corrected in `Style_Anchor_Registry.json` with the evidence note inline.
3. **Activities expressed without a widget keyword** (BLL phonics 1A/1C/1D: `[Activity N]` + instructions + data TABLE, type only in prose) now bundle as **unclassified** widgets — captured un-built in the distinct container + manifest entry + red flag ("widget type must be identified"), never rendered as a plain content table (`InteractiveScanner` activity-with-table trigger; members collected via the shared `#swallowMembers`).
4. **The "half-wrapped" 1E:** two placeholder bugs — opener items (the activity's own title/instruction lines) were consumed but never rendered (text LOST), and the placeholder emitted inside the still-open previous activity div. Placeholders now render opener content first, and a bundle that is itself a new `[Activity N]` closes any open activity (the bank's absolute-terminator rule) before emitting.
5. New lexicon tag **`supervisor note`** (CONTAINER_OPEN; BLL146's `[supervisor note]` previously embedded-matched the supervisor BUTTON alias and rendered the note text as a button label) + the gold `row supervisor > super-content` structure as an `own_row` callout template (`Emit_Templates`).

**BLL146 after the fixes:** 3/3 pages, menu holds the Understand/Know/Do block, `<h3>Introduction</h3>` + supervisor structure + welcome in the body, activities 1A/1C/1D/1E all captured (3 unclassified + 1 dragAndDrop) with no lost text and no nesting; acks 27/29 human entries reproduced. **Full corpus re-run (188 converted; TRR106+TRR114 both now refused by design):** exact wrapper chains 85.3%, over-nesting 2.1%, captured interactives 5,805 (the unclassified class adds ~900 flagged build-tasks). Gates green after the lexicon/registry edits (Python 99.99%, JS 100%). Note: the rows-ratio AVERAGE (5.8×) is skewed by tiny-denominator single-file pages; the per-block row policy is unchanged from round 3.

## 2026-06-12 (round 3) — Gold-standard containment + per-block rows (the OSAI201 fix)

Driven by Chris's OSAI201 spot-check: everything after a `[whakatauki]` was nesting inside it. Root cause: callout containment violated the project's own marker model (§1.1 — a marker's content is the black text following it, up to the NEXT marker); the auto-close list only reacted to headings/structural tags, never to `[body]`/`[video]`. The earlier comparison HAD counted this class (387 cases) and I mis-triaged it as ambiguity — wrong call, now fixed at the root.

**Evidence mined from ALL 2,045 human pages (recorded in the data files):** `.whakatauki` holds ONLY its proverb `<p>`s (median 2, n=181), 179/181 split "reo | english" into two `<p>`s; 51% of all rows hold exactly one direct child (one-structure-per-row is the dominant convention); youtube-nocookie is the dominant embed host (885 vs 473); the whakataukī icon img is current practice (signed-off OSAI201) though 0/181 in this archive.

**Changes:**
1. **Strict callout containment** (`ContentConverter.#calloutOpen` + `Emit_Templates callouts.containment`): a callout holds only its own content run and is emitted complete — never on the stack — so no following tag can nest inside it. ONE exception: an explicit matching `[end X]` ahead switches to SPAN mode (writer-authored box, closed only by their end tag / section / page boundary). Generic closers (`[End Phase 1]` → "end other") deliberately do NOT count as span evidence (TEFUN07 regression caught and fixed).
2. **Per-block rows** (`Emit_Templates body_region.row_breaks` mode "per-block"): every root-level block in its own `div.row`; a heading keeps its immediately-following text run (the corpus's heading+paragraph rows).
3. **Whakataukī**: pipe-split into two `<p>`s + the `whakataukiImg` icon in the open template (data).
4. **Video host** → `youtube-nocookie.com` (data).
5. **Lexicon**: + aliases `alert box ends here` / `alert ends here` for `end alert` (MXDB302's close phrasing opened NEW alerts via the embedded "alert box" match). One-alias fix, per the extension contract.

**Results (188 modules, 4,448 matched elements):** exact wrapper chain 79.7% → **85.4%** (+6.7% same-set = 92.1%); over-nesting 8.8% → **2.3%** (387 → 101); OSAI201 now 0 over-nested, rows_ratio 0.94, structure matching the gold example block-for-block. Remaining 2.3% + the 4.4% under-nesting are writer/dev judgment divergence (devs adding/removing boxes the source doesn't mark), itemised per module in `structural_comparison.json`. Rows ratio overall 2.75× human (we split per-block everywhere; humans group ~half the time — visual-only difference, the chains score row+col identically). Gates after every edit: Python 99.99%, JS 100%.

A change to an element present in just some modules (e.g. a widget) regenerates only the modules that contain it — in the WT or any HTML page — and then all of that module's pages; a change to an always-present concern (skeleton, header, menu, body wrappers, footer, acks, image mode, tag normalisation) regenerates every module. Use `reference/tests/regen_affected.cjs "<rendered-class>" "[source-tag]"` (or `--all`) to compute the set and the rebuild command, then re-run the gates.

## 2026-06-12 — Findings + fixes during real-module verification

Every fix below was driven by a real corpus observation, and recorded as data where the knowledge belongs:

1. **Google-Docs pagination**: writers' docx files carry `w:pageBreakBefore w:val="0"` (meaning NO break) on nearly every paragraph and often zero `lastRenderedPageBreak` records → WT page numbers are untrustworthy. Added `Input_Doc_Rules.media_item_lesson_mapping` (evidence chain: content URL/ID match → page records when trustworthy → neighbour interpolation → loud fallback) and `wt_page_tracking.min_pages_for_trust`.
2. **MTK signature false-positive**: "MTK WRITERS TEMPLATE" appears in STANDARD templates' front-matter (OSAH401) → unsupported-pathway rule now also requires the TRR code prefix (`also_requires_code_prefix`).
3. **Fundamentals openers**: ARFUN01/MXFUN03/EXPFUN04 have no `[TITLE BAR]` — content-start detection chain extended with `content_start_canonicals` (`title bar`, `lesson content`) + loud no-opener fallback.
4. **Implicit page breaks are normal**: ANZH205 opens five of its seven lessons with just `[end page]` + `[H2] Lesson N:` — the splitter harvests the lesson number/title from the heading (info note, not a warning).
5. **BLL `[PAGE]`-as-lesson**: `[PAGE]` straight after the overview (or after another such page) numbers as successive lessons (BLL233 = -00/-01/-02), while `[PAGE]` inside a lesson sub-numbers (x.1).
6. **Registry `page_model` beats the no-lesson-tags heuristic**: XGF9001 has NO `[LESSON]` tags yet is multi-file purely via `[End page]` (registry: multi-file) — the heuristic now only applies when the registry is silent.
7. **Media-list hyperlinks captured per ROW** (`block.rowLinks`) — a pooled-links version matched every iStock row to the first URL in the table.
8. **Render content is never case-folded**: added `TagNormaliser.RenderText()` to pull embedded titles in their ORIGINAL case (`[Insert H3: Emotion]` → "Emotion"); used by headings, callout titles, buttons, lesson titles, menu headings (took ARFUN01 from 0/5 to 5/5 headings found).
9. **Interactives inside table rows** (speech-bubble pattern 8) detected by scanning table cells' red spans.
10. Data edits along the way: `Acks_Formats.special_tokens` — removed `it`/`id` (ordinary words in titles).
